addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Proxy-side background messages were reworked 2026-07-29 but never verified against a running proxy. Two behaviors to confirm live: (1) a terminating background task reaches the model as the wake-up text, not as a bare '.' — the role='system' plain-str delivery shape was previously nuked; (2) both the launch-ack and the termination message carry three lines: message, 'Output: <path>', 'ID: <task id>'. Code merged, 119/119 regression checks pass, no live run.

# Replaced bg message renders across two lines, only the tail is green
State: OPEN | #52
Author: brunowinter8192
Created: 2026-07-29T17:45:54Z | Updated: 2026-07-29T17:45:54Z
Labels: proxy
Comments: 0
URL: https://github.com/brunowinter8192/monitor-cc/issues/52

---

What it is:
When the proxy replaces a background-launch ack, the pane renders the result across two lines: the shared leading word sits unhighlighted on its own line, the replacement text follows on a green line below. Cause is the span computation in rule_ops.py::_extract_block_op — it strips the common prefix/suffix of old vs new text, so a replacement sharing its first word with the original is recorded as a partial span; render_messages.py then emits each span on its own line. Desired: the replacement renders as one contiguous, fully green line.

Note the 2026-07-29 rework changed the replacement text (now three lines incl. ID) — re-observe the current rendering before assuming the old shape.

Area: proxy_instrumentation  (-> process-docs/proxy_instrumentation/, dev/proxy_instrumentation/)

Resume: RAG search "strip inject span common prefix render line split" on monitor-cc-docs --document 'process-docs/proxy_instrumentation/%'
==========
# Proxy strips quoted system-reminder blocks out of our own tool output (data loss)
State: OPEN | #46
Author: brunowinter8192
Created: 2026-07-28T00:10:58Z | Updated: 2026-07-28T00:10:58Z
Labels: proxy
Comments: 0
URL: https://github.com/brunowinter8192/monitor-cc/issues/46

---

What it is:
The SR strip passes match on line-anchored <system-reminder> blocks regardless of WHERE the segment came from. A block quoted inside our own tool output — RAG result text, a GitHub issue body, a process-doc, a strings dump of the CC binary — sits at line start when fenced in markdown, so the anchor guard does not protect it. The proxy removes it before the payload reaches the model: the agent asks for the content and never sees the part it asked about.

Confirmed on the 2026-07-28 dual-log corpus by replaying real tool_result segments through the real pipeline: 2 segments stripped, mods stripped_task_tools_nag and stripped_all_sr_msg0 + stripped_git_lock_advice, removing quoted SR text and a quoted git-lock advice block out of retrieved reference material.

Scope: decide how a strip pass distinguishes CC-authored injection from content WE pulled in. Candidates include gating SR strips out of tool_result segments entirely (mirrors strip_sn_notice.py, which already does top-level-only traversal), or an origin check on the enclosing block. Note strip_hook_prefix / strip_git_lock legitimately need tool_result descent, so this is not a blanket rule.

Area: strip_fp_tool_result  (-> process-docs/strip_fp_tool_result/, dev/strip_fp_tool_result/)

Resume: RAG search "quoted system-reminder tool_result false positive strip origin" on monitor-cc-docs --document 'process-docs/strip_fp_tool_result/%'

📋 Phase 1 — Step 1: Session Scope

> - Repo `monitor-cc`, Branch `main`, Remote `brunowinter8192/monitor-cc`
> - Issue-Bodies #51, #52, #46 gelesen
> - Git-Log 27.–31. Juli gesichtet: die Fixes `cf53c52` (role=system Wake-up), `ad3c3b8` (Task-ID in beiden Meldungen), `66a24bc` (Span-Rendering) und `05cbf99` (SR-Strip steigt nicht mehr in tool_result ab) sitzen alle auf `main`

**Diese Sitzung verifiziert drei bereits gebaute Fixes am laufenden Proxy — gebaut wird zunächst nichts.**
Alle drei Issues haben denselben Status: Code gemerged, Regressionstests grün, aber nie gegen einen echten laufenden Proxy geprüft. Der frisch gestartete Proxy dieser Sitzung trägt den Stand vom 28./29. Juli, also ist die Prüfung jetzt möglich und war es vorher nicht.

import re

# INFRASTRUCTURE

# Fast-path marker — cheap contains check before block walk
_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_MARKER = 'running in background with ID'
# Anchored ack prefix: a genuine CC bg-launch ack ALWAYS starts with this exact prefix. The strip
# decision uses startswith() on the lstripped text (NOT substring-anywhere), so a large tool_result
# or user message that merely CONTAINS the phrase as data is never destroyed (was the FP-nuke bug).
_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_PREFIX = 'Command running in background with ID:'

_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_MSG = (
    'Command is running in the background. Do NOT check, poll, or read its output — '
    'just wait until it finishes (you will get a completion notice).'
)

# Recover id/path FROM the ack text being replaced — real recorded shape (verified against
# src/logs/dual_log/): "Command running in background with ID: <id>. Output is being written to:
# <path>. You will be notified when it completes. To check interim output, use Read on that file
# path." Id group excludes '.' (ids are alnum tokens in every measured occurrence); path group is
# non-greedy up to the literal ". You will be notified" so an internal dot in the path (e.g. the
# ".output" extension) doesn't truncate it early.
_ACK_ID_RE = re.compile(r'Command running in background with ID:\s*([^.]*)\.')
_ACK_PATH_RE = re.compile(r'Output is being written to:\s*(.*?)\.\s*You will be notified', re.DOTALL)


# True only for a genuine bg-launch ack: the marker phrase anchored at the start of the text.
def _is_bg_launch_ack(text):
    return text.lstrip().startswith(_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_PREFIX)


# ORCHESTRATOR

# Replace entire content of any block whose text STARTS WITH the bg-launch-ack prefix with the
# 3-line hold message (msg + optional Output: + optional ID:, recovered from the ack itself).
# Anchored (not substring-anywhere): legitimate content that merely contains the phrase is kept.
# Covers all 4 content shapes: str, list[text], list[tool_result+str], list[tool_result+list].
# Returns (new_content, removed_chunks) — removed_chunks: original texts of replaced blocks.
def _strip_bg_launch_ack(content):
    removed = []
    if isinstance(content, str):
        if _is_bg_launch_ack(content):
            removed.append(content)
            return _build_launch_ack_replacement(content), removed
        return content, removed
    if isinstance(content, list):
        result = []
        for block in content:
            if not isinstance(block, dict):
                result.append(block)
                continue
            btype = block.get('type')
            if btype == 'text':
                text = block.get('text', '')
                if _is_bg_launch_ack(text):
                    removed.append(text)
                    result.append({**block, 'text': _build_launch_ack_replacement(text)})
                else:
                    result.append(block)
            elif btype == 'tool_result':
                inner = block.get('content', '')
                if isinstance(inner, str):
                    if _is_bg_launch_ack(inner):
                        removed.append(inner)
                        result.append({**block, 'content': _build_launch_ack_replacement(inner)})
                    else:
                        result.append(block)
                elif isinstance(inner, list):
                    new_sub = []
                    sub_changed = False
                    for sub in inner:
                        if isinstance(sub, dict) and sub.get('type') == 'text':
                            text = sub.get('text', '')
                            if _is_bg_launch_ack(text):
                                removed.append(text)
                                new_sub.append({**sub, 'text': _build_launch_ack_replacement(text)})
                                sub_changed = True
                            else:
                                new_sub.append(sub)
                        else:
                            new_sub.append(sub)
                    result.append({**block, 'content': new_sub} if sub_changed else block)
                else:
                    result.append(block)
            else:
                result.append(block)
        return result, removed
    return content, removed


# FUNCTIONS

# Build the 3-line hold message from a genuine ack's text: msg, then Output: <path> (if the ack's
# path was recovered), then ID: <id> (if the ack's id was recovered). A value that fails to extract
# is OMITTED — never "ID: None", never a dangling "ID:" with nothing after it. Not observed in real
# data (id+path present in every measured ack), defensive only.
def _build_launch_ack_replacement(ack_text):
    id_match = _ACK_ID_RE.search(ack_text)
    path_match = _ACK_PATH_RE.search(ack_text)
    task_id = id_match.group(1).strip() if id_match else ''
    path = path_match.group(1).strip() if path_match else ''
    lines = [_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_MSG]
    if path:
        lines.append('Output: ' + path)
    if task_id:
        lines.append('ID: ' + task_id)
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'

1	# tool_result SR-Strip FP Audit — Measurement Only, 2026-07-28
2	
3	Same FP-nuke class as `bg_launch_ack_anchor.md` / `rs_pass_truncation_notice.md` in this area:
4	a strip pass's marker matching descends into `tool_result` content and can fire on QUOTED data
5	(RAG results, file Reads, docs describing the strip itself) instead of a genuine per-request CC
6	injection. This session scoped the question specifically to the `<system-reminder>`-template
7	family (`strip_sr.py`) and measured, rather than assumed, how often that specific family actually
8	fires inside `tool_result` across five real dual-log sessions (`api_requests_opus_monitor_cc`,
9	`api_requests_opus_posts`, `api_requests_opus_wise2627` [2.2GB], `api_requests_worker_*_pdf-refs`,
10	`api_requests_worker_*_capture-monitor-cc-ref`; a sixth file, this worker's own live
11	`sr-fp-audit` session log, was excluded by name — its own Read/Bash calls on this investigation
12	would otherwise masquerade as evidence).
13	
14	## Method
15	
16	Threaded the 11 real `_apply_*` pass functions from `message_passes.py` through every payload's
17	messages in `rules.py::apply_modification_rules`'s exact order, using each pass's own per-block
18	diff (`pass_ops_by_msg_blk`) to attribute a removal to a specific `(msg_idx, blk_idx)` and check
19	that block's PRE-pass `type`. Only removals landing on a `type == 'tool_result'` block count.
20	Deduplicated per `(file, exact removed text)` — dual-logs are cumulative snapshots, the same
21	message reappears in every later request of a session. Template classification used `strip_sr.py`'s
22	own `_match_template`/`_ENV_CONTEXT_RE`/`_IMP_LINE_RE` registries (imported, not reinvented).
23	Quoted-vs-genuine verdicts were written by hand after reviewing each occurrence's tool_use origin
24	(resolved `tool_use_id → tool name/input` from the payload's own assistant blocks) and surrounding
25	context (fence-parity signal: odd `` ``` `` count before the removal = inside an open fence).
26	
27	## Result — split by pass family (the critical correction this session made)
28	
29	30 tool_result-level removals total, but pooling them into one number is wrong: 3 of the 11 passes
30	(`_apply_first_pass`'s SR branches, `_apply_cumulative_sr_strips`, `_apply_final_sr_pass`) actually
31	import and match through `strip_sr.py`; the other 3 that fired here (`_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip`,
32	`_apply_hook_prefix_strip`, `_apply_po_preview_strip`) match their own, unrelated markers and never
33	touch `strip_sr.py` at all. An early draft of the audit report pooled all 30 into "28 genuine CC
34	injections found inside tool_result, the fix must not blanket-disable descent" — true for the pool,
35	but the pooled 29 (after final corpus growth) were ALL non-SR-family (real hook-error prefixes, real
36	background-launch acks, real persisted-output previews on genuinely oversized Bash output — all
37	correctly matching their own markers, out of this issue's scope). Split by family:
38	
39	- **SR strip family: 1 tool_result-level occurrence in the entire corpus.** A `rag-cli search`
40	  over `monitor-cc-docs` (querying this exact bug) returned a process-docs paragraph that fences a
41	  literal, real-newline example of the env-context system-reminder block ("CC injects this SR
42	  block on nearly every request:\n```\n<the block>\n```\n334 chars..."), and `_apply_first_pass`
43	  stripped it out of the tool_result as if it were a live per-request injection. Confirmed false
44	  positive — `fence_odd_before = True`, i.e. the removed text sits between a matched open/close
45	  markdown fence pair, the concrete signal available to distinguish this from genuine content.
46	  **0 genuine SR-family injections found** in ~660 requests across 5 real sessions — a thin (n=1)
47	  sample, backed by the structural argument that CC injects these fixed SR templates into
48	  top-level user-message text, never as part of another tool's own return value, but explicitly
49	  not "structurally impossible", just "no counter-example found here".
50	- **Non-SR passes: 29 occurrences, all genuine, all out of this issue's scope.**
51	
52	## Ground-truth non-reproduction (reported honestly, not smoothed over)
53	
54	The task's stated ground truth (a prior session's 2-segment finding: `stripped_task_tools_nag` +
55	`stripped_all_sr_msg0` + `stripped_git_lock_advice`, "quoted SR text and a quoted git-lock advice
56	block out of retrieved reference material") did NOT reproduce as an actual strip in this corpus
57	snapshot. Built a reusable check (`_scan_ground_truth_git_lock`): 33 requests carry the git-lock
58	marker substring inside a `tool_result`, 0 are literal matches of the real 5-line advice block
59	(real newlines) — every hit is `strip_git_lock.py`'s own escaped source code (`\n` as two literal
60	characters in the .py file, which the exact-substring strip never matches, by construction) or
61	prose mentioning the marker. The only place the literal block was found at all was this worker's
62	own excluded self-session log, as an artifact of investigating `strip_git_lock.py` itself — not
63	production evidence. Plausible explanation: the dual-log directory is a rolling window (already
64	documented in `dev/proxy/replay_sn_notice_strip.py`'s own prior count-divergence finding), so the
65	snapshot behind the original 2-segment finding likely rotated out before this measurement.
66	
67	## Artifacts
68	
69	Script + full occurrence-level report: `dev/strip_fp_tool_result/audit_tool_result_sr_strips.py`,
70	`dev/strip_fp_tool_result/md/audit_tool_result_sr_strips.md` (per-occurrence template, tool,
71	verbatim text, file+line, verdict+evidence; aggregate split by family).
72	
73	## Implication for the next milestone
74	
75	What the data supports: for the SR strip family specifically, `tool_result` descent produced 0
76	genuine strips and 1 false positive across ~660 requests — no measured case where descent
77	delivered any value. Per-pass non-descent is already the established pattern in this codebase, not
78	a novel proposal: `_apply_sn_notice_strip` and `_apply_bg_exit_strip` both deliberately skip
79	`tool_result` entirely, with the rationale recorded in their own source comments. Dropping SR-family
80	descent would extend an existing, precedented pattern to three more passes, not invent one.
81	
82	What remains open: whether to drop SR-family `tool_result` descent outright or gate it some other
83	way. The n=1 sample means this is a judgment call for the next milestone, not a number-driven
84	conclusion — the measurement rules out "descent is currently earning its keep" but does not by
85	itself prove "descent can never matter". The fence-parity signal (odd `` ``` `` count before the
86	removed text) was useful EVIDENCE for hand-classifying this one occurrence; it is not proposed as a
87	runtime discriminator — counting fence markers breaks on tilde fences, nested/indented fences,
88	unbalanced fences in retrieved documents, and prose that merely mentions a fence.
89	
90	Separate from all of this: the non-SR passes' (`bg_launch_ack`, `hook_prefix`, `po_preview`)
91	`tool_result` descent is correct, necessary, and untouched by this question — none of the above
92	implications apply to them.

> - `strip_bg_launch_ack.py` gelesen: Ersetzung hängt an dem exakten Präfix `Command running in background with ID:`
> - `grep "manually backgrounded"` über `src/proxy` → 0 Treffer
> - `rule_ops.py::_extract_block_op` gelesen: schneidet gemeinsamen Präfix/Suffix ab
> - Prozess-Doku mit eingebettetem Erinnerungsblock über das Lesewerkzeug gezogen (Testfall #46)

**#46 ist bestätigt behoben — der zitierte Block kam vollständig bei mir an.**
Ich habe eine Prozess-Doku gelesen, in der so ein Erinnerungsblock wörtlich als Beispiel eingebettet ist, zeilenbündig und damit genau in der Form, die der Proxy früher herausgeschnitten hat. Alle neun Zeilen des Blocks sind angekommen, inklusive der Mailadresse und des Datums darin. Das ist eine echte Live-Beobachtung, kein Codeurteil: ich war der Empfänger.

**#51 ist zur Hälfte bestätigt — die Beendigungsmeldung stimmt, und zwar auf beiden Wegen.**
Sowohl bei der Schleife, die du manuell in den Hintergrund geschoben hast, als auch beim Timer, den ich selbst im Hintergrund gestartet habe, kam die Weckmeldung als saubere Dreizeilerform an: Meldung, Ausgabepfad, Kennung. Kein nacktes Satzzeichen. Damit ist der Kern von #51 erledigt.

**Die zweite Hälfte von #51 fällt beim manuell verschobenen Aufruf durch — und der Grund ist im Code eindeutig.**
Die Ersetzung hängt an einem wörtlichen Textanfang: „Command running in background with ID:". Claude Code schreibt beim manuellen Verschieben aber „Command was manually backgrounded by user with ID:". Der Vergleich schlägt fehl, es wird nichts ersetzt, und beim Modell landet der Originaltext mit der Kennung mitten im Fließsatz. Die Suche nach dem Wort „manually backgrounded" im gesamten Proxy-Code liefert null Treffer — dieser Startweg ist schlicht nie implementiert worden. Das ist Tatsache, nicht Vermutung.

**#52 ist bestätigt nicht behoben, und dein Bild zeigt exakt den vorhergesagten Mechanismus.**
Original und Ersatztext beginnen beide mit demselben Wort „Command". Die Spannenberechnung schneidet genau diese Gemeinsamkeit vorne ab, meldet also nur den Rest als geändert — deshalb steht „Command" blass auf eigener Zeile und der grüne Block beginnt erst darunter mit „is running in the background". Der Fehler ist der gemeinsame Präfixabgleich in der Spannenberechnung, nicht die Darstellung selbst. Beim Beendigungsfall tritt er nicht auf, weil dort kein gemeinsamer Wortanfang existiert.

**Offen bleibt der dritte Startweg: der Aufruf, den Claude Code nach Zeitüberschreitung selbst in den Hintergrund schiebt.**
Dafür brauche ich einen Befehl, der die Zeitgrenze reißt — meinen Versuch dazu hast du abgebrochen. Sag mir, ob ich den nochmal ansetzen soll, dann haben wir alle drei Wege vermessen, bevor wir irgendetwas bauen.

Extracted the span-emitting logic (new-format inline tuples vs. legacy stacked yellow/green) out

branches (`_render_new_messages`, `_render_modified_messages`) now call these at block index
`"0"` — confirmed against the recorded payload that block-less messages are always logged at
coordinate `"0"`, not assumed. `highlight_suspect=False` is passed from the block-less callers
specifically so the fix does not retroactively add suspect-tag highlighting to plain content that
never had it before — the bug was missing span color, not missing tag highlighting, and scope
was kept to exactly that.

## Line-number correction

The prior observation recorded the reproduction at dual-log line 133. The data is actually at
line 132 (0-based) — resolved by matching `request_id b6e4f411-74b2-4b56-8940-bf5ce51e7380`

Nur stammten alle zwölf aus dem selbst gestarteten Weg — der manuell verschobene kam im Messkorpus schlicht nicht vor. Die Erkennung wurde also korrekt auf das gebaut, was messbar war, und ist genau deshalb blind für die zweite Form. Derselbe Eintrag sagt außerdem ausdrücklich, was nicht geprüft wurde: ein echter Proxy-Neustart mit echtem Hintergrund-Task. Das ist die Prüfung, die wir heute nachgeholt haben.

**Der gemeinsame Präfixabgleich ist kein Versehen, sondern gewollt — und trotzdem an dieser Stelle falsch.**
Er dient dazu, kleine Änderungen eng zu markieren, statt einen ganzen Block grün einzufärben. Bei einer Vollersetzung, die zufällig mit demselben Wort beginnt, kippt dieses Verhalten ins Gegenteil. Die Vorgängersitzung hat an dieser Datei bereits gearbeitet, aber an einer anderen Ursache: dort ging es darum, dass die Anzeige die Spannen gar nicht erst nachschlug, wenn der Inhalt kein Blocklistenformat mehr hatte. Das ist behoben — die Farben erscheinen jetzt. Nur der Zuschnitt der Spanne stimmt nicht.

Die Zuordnung einer Ersetzung zu der Funktion, die sie verursacht hat, rät anhand eines geteilten Satzes statt die tatsächlich gelaufene Funktion zu verfolgen. Das ist bekannt, bewusst nicht gefixt und bleibt auch heute liegen — du hast #50 ausgenommen.

# Emit strip/inject-highlighted content lines for one block or block-less message body.
# Dispatches new-format inline render (i_blk holds (tag, text) tuples) vs legacy stacked
# render (full_text in DIM, then s_blk chunks in yellow, then i_blk chunks in green).
# indent: leading whitespace — block path nests one level deeper than block-less messages.
# highlight_suspect: apply _SUSPECT_TAG_RE to the plain (no-span) full_text render — True for
# the block path (existing behavior, preserved exactly); False for block-less callers, whose
# plain-content rendering never highlighted suspect tags before this fix and must not start now.
def _render_span_content(full_text: str, i_blk: list, s_blk: list, indent: str, highlight_suspect: bool = True) -> tuple:
    lines = []
    keys = []
    if i_blk and isinstance(i_blk[0], (list, tuple)):
        # New format: inline render — equal=DIM, injected=DIM_GREEN_BG, no gray preview
        for tag, span_text in i_blk:
            bg = DIM_GREEN_BG if tag == "injected" else ""
            for raw_line in span_text.split('\n'):
                raw_line = raw_line.expandtabs(8)
                if not raw_line:
                    lines.append(f"{indent}{bg}{DIM}{SOFT_RESET}")
                    keys.append(None)
                    continue
                highlighted = _SUSPECT_TAG_RE.sub(
                    lambda m: f'{LIGHT_RED_BG}{m.group(0)}{RESET}{DIM}', raw_line
                )
                lines.append(f"{indent}{bg}{DIM}{highlighted}{SOFT_RESET}")
                keys.append(None)
        for span_text in s_blk:
            for raw_line in span_text.split('\n'):
                raw_line = raw_line.expandtabs(8)
                lines.append(f"{indent}{DIM_YELLOW_BG}{DIM}{raw_line or ''}{SOFT_RESET}")
                keys.append(None)
    else:
        if full_text:
            for raw_line in full_text.split('\n'):
                raw_line = raw_line.expandtabs(8)
                if not raw_line:
                    lines.append(f"{indent}{DIM}{SOFT_RESET}")
                    keys.append(None)
                    continue
                line_out = (
                    _SUSPECT_TAG_RE.sub(lambda m: f'{LIGHT_RED_BG}{m.group(0)}{RESET}{DIM}', raw_line)
                    if highlight_suspect else raw_line
                )
                lines.append(f"{indent}{DIM}{line_out}{SOFT_RESET}")
                keys.append(None)
        for span_text in s_blk:
            for raw_line in span_text.split('\n'):
                raw_line = raw_line.expandtabs(8)
                lines.append(f"{indent}{DIM_YELLOW_BG}{DIM}{raw_line or ''}{SOFT_RESET}")
                keys.append(None)
        for span_text in i_blk:
            for raw_line in span_text.split('\n'):
                raw_line = raw_line.expandtabs(8)
                lines.append(f"{indent}{DIM_GREEN_BG}{DIM}{raw_line or ''}{SOFT_RESET}")
                keys.append(None)
    return lines, keys

# Look up the (injected, stripped) span lists recorded for one message/block coordinate.
# Returns ([], []) when use_dual is False (legacy log — no dual-log spans available).
def _lookup_spans(entry: dict, msg_idx: int, bidx, use_dual: bool) -> tuple:
    if not use_dual:
        return [], []
    i_blk = entry['_injected_spans']['messages'].get(str(msg_idx), {}).get(str(bidx)) or []
    s_blk = entry['_stripped_spans']['messages'].get(str(msg_idx), {}).get(str(bidx)) or []
    return i_blk, s_blk

📋 Phase 1 — Step 3: Code Investigation & Gap Analysis

> - Gelesen: `rule_ops.py` (58 LOC), `strip_bg_launch_ack.py` (107), `message_passes.py` Ack-Durchlauf 444-468, `strip_inject_delta.py` (296), `render_messages.py` 60-129, `diff_engine.py::compose_block`, `payload_helpers.py::_content_contains`, `strip_vocab.py` BL-Eintrag
> - Testbestand gesichtet: `dev/proxy/test_strip_fix.py` (776 Zeilen), `dev/proxy_dual_log/proxy_176_bg_launch_ack_tests.py`

**Die zweite Startform scheitert an drei Stellen hintereinander, nicht an einer.**
Erstens filtert eine Schnellprüfung vor: sie sucht die Wortfolge „running in background with ID", die in der manuellen Form gar nicht vorkommt — der Durchlauf bricht sofort ab. Zweitens prüft die eigentliche Erkennung auf den Textanfang „Command running in background with ID:". Drittens holt sich die Pfaderkennung den Ausgabepfad, indem sie bis zum Satz „You will be notified" liest — und dieser Satz fehlt in der manuellen Form komplett. Ich habe nachgemessen: der manuelle Text ist exakt 220 Zeichen lang und endet direkt nach dem Pfad. Die Zahl deckt sich mit der Blockgröße in deinem Fenster, also zwei unabhängige Belege. Eine Reparatur, die nur den Textanfang ergänzt, würde die Kennungszeile liefern, aber die Pfadzeile stillschweigend weglassen.

**Der Spannenzuschnitt hat genau einen Verursacher, und der wird von siebzehn Stellen benutzt.**
Die Berechnung sitzt in einer einzigen kleinen Funktion, die von siebzehn Durchläufen aufgerufen wird. Jede Änderung daran trifft also alle Ersetzungen, nicht nur die Startbestätigung. Das ist der eigentliche Risikopunkt der ganzen Sitzung: das enge Markieren ist für echte Teiländerungen richtig und soll es bleiben. Nur wenn ein Durchlauf den gesamten Inhalt ersetzt, ist das Wegschneiden des gemeinsamen Wortanfangs irreführend.

**Gap 1 — schließt eine Messung: wie viele der siebzehn Aufrufer ersetzen vollständig?**
Ohne diese Zahl weiß niemand, ob eine Änderung an der gemeinsamen Funktion drei oder fünfzehn Darstellungen umfärbt. Die Antwort steckt in den aufgezeichneten Verkehrsdaten, die im Projekt liegen — ein Prüfskript kann alle bisherigen Spannen durchrechnen und beide Varianten gegenüberstellen. Das ist Arbeit für den Arbeiter, nicht für dich.

**Gap 2 — schließt eine Messung: kommt die manuelle Startform in den Altdaten überhaupt vor?**
Mein Versuch, sie aus den Protokollen zu ziehen, lieferte nur Rauschen — Treffer aus meiner eigenen laufenden Sitzung und aus Binärmüll. Belastbar ist bisher nur die eine Beobachtung von heute Abend. Vor dem Bauen sollte ein sauberer Suchlauf über die Aufzeichnungen bestätigen, dass es genau diese eine Form gibt und keine vierte Variante mit anderem Wortlaut.

**Externe Quellen: eine wäre nützlich, ist aber nicht kritisch.**
Der Wortlaut der Meldungen stammt aus Claude Code selbst, ist also nirgends offiziell dokumentiert — die einzige verlässliche Quelle sind unsere eigenen Aufzeichnungen und eine Zeichenkettensuche in der Programmdatei von Claude Code. Letztere würde alle Varianten auf einen Schlag liefern, statt sie einzeln zu erjagen. Falls du das für sinnvoll hältst, sag Bescheid; sonst reicht mir der Messkorpus. Von außerhalb des Projekts brauche ich nichts.

**Ein Nebenbefund, den ich nicht anfasse.**
Die Zuordnung, welche Funktion eine Ersetzung verursacht hat, rät bei der Startbestätigung anhand desselben Wortlauts, der auch die Erkennung steuert. Wenn ein zweiter Wortlaut dazukommt, muss dieses Vokabular mitgepflegt werden, sonst steht im Fenster eine falsche Funktionsangabe. Das gehört zum Bauauftrag dazu — es ist nicht dasselbe wie Issue #50, das eine andere, tiefere Ungenauigkeit betrifft und liegen bleibt.

🛑 Anmerkungen? Sonst gehe ich zu Schritt 4 und schneide die Meilensteine.

content.text:
📋 Phase 1 — Step 4: Deliverables & Milestones

**Das Ganze: zwei unabhängige Defekte, gemessen bevor gebaut wird, in drei Meilensteinen.**
Erst wird vermessen, was die Erkennung heute übersieht und wie weit eine Änderung am Spannenzuschnitt ausstrahlt. Erst danach wird an beiden Stellen gebaut — getrennt, weil sie verschiedene Dateien und verschiedene Risiken haben. Der Spannenzuschnitt kommt zuletzt, weil er die gemeinsame Funktion aller siebzehn Ersetzungen berührt und deshalb die belastbarste Messung braucht.

**Meilenstein 1 — Messung beider Lücken, kein Produktivcode.**
Ein Prüfskript unter `dev/bg_wakeup_id_line/` sucht in den aufgezeichneten Verkehrsdaten alle Startbestätigungen und listet die vorkommenden Wortlaute mit Häufigkeit auf — die Frage ist, ob es genau zwei Formen gibt oder mehr. Ein zweites unter `dev/proxy_instrumentation/` rechnet alle aufgezeichneten Ersetzungen einmal mit dem heutigen und einmal mit einem vollersetzungs-bewussten Zuschnitt durch und zählt, wie viele Darstellungen sich ändern würden.
Nachweis: beide Berichte liegen als Datei in `md/` unter ihrem Bereich, mit konkreten Zahlen und Stichprobengröße. Ich lese sie und prüfe, ob die Zahlen die Annahmen tragen.

**Meilenstein 2 — Erkennung der manuell verschobenen Startbestätigung.**
Betrifft `strip_bg_launch_ack.py` und die Schnellprüfung in `message_passes.py`, dazu das Attributionsvokabular in `strip_vocab.py`. Die zweite Form muss den Dreizeiler genauso erzeugen wie die erste — inklusive Pfadzeile, obwohl der abschließende Satz fehlt, an dem die heutige Pfaderkennung hängt.
Nachweis: die bestehende Prüfsammlung läuft vollständig durch, plus neue Prüfungen, die den echten 220-Zeichen-Text von heute Abend wörtlich festnageln. Danach starte ich zur Kontrolle einen echten Hintergrund-Task, den du manuell verschiebst — das ist der Live-Beleg, und dafür brauche ich dich.

**Meilenstein 3 — Spannenzuschnitt bei Vollersetzung.**
Betrifft `rule_ops.py`, gestützt auf die Zahlen aus Meilenstein 1. Ziel: eine Ersetzung, die den ganzen Inhalt austauscht, wird als eine zusammenhängende Spanne geführt statt um den gemeinsamen Wortanfang beschnitten. Enge Markierung bei echten Teiländerungen bleibt unverändert.
Nachweis: die Prüfsammlungen laufen durch, und ein Wiedergabelauf gegen echte aufgezeichnete Daten zeigt die Startbestätigung als eine durchgehende Spanne. Die letzte Instanz bist du: im Proxy-Fenster muss die ersetzte Meldung als ein durchgehend grüner Block stehen, ohne blasses „Command" davor.

**Was ausdrücklich nicht dazugehört.**
Issue #50 zur Etikettierung bleibt unangetastet. Der dritte Startweg existiert nicht — Claude Code bricht bei Zeitüberschreitung ab, statt in den Hintergrund zu schieben; das wird beim Aktualisieren der Dokumentation festgehalten, nicht gebaut.

🛑 Anmerkungen? Sonst spawne ich den Arbeiter für Meilenstein 1.

worker-cli send bg-ack-shapes "Two of your three points: Go as proposed. One needs correcting before you implement.

GO as-is:
- Corpus + exclusion set + the structural 'block text starts with Command at position 0' filter INSTEAD of blanket file exclusion — this is better than what I specified, keep it. Your finding that wording B occurs in the real corpus (monitor_cc_1785336796, same toolu_id repeated across ~90 cumulative lines) is exactly the kind of result that had to be measured rather than assumed.
- Dedup via prev_msg_count slicing, mechanism verdicts by importing the real symbols: correct.
- The _apply_role_system_strip observation (content -> '.'; an original ending in '.' gets that char absorbed as common suffix, leaving the injected span EMPTY) is a genuine second finding. Surface it in the report as its own flagged case with its corpus count.

CORRECT THIS — D2 classification must not rest on a magic threshold:
'ratio = len(removed)/len(bt) >= 0.85 -> FULL' is a PROXY for the property that actually matters, and it can misclassify in both directions. A partial excision can legitimately remove >85% of a block (a large SR block inside a message with little other text is exactly that shape), and a full replacement whose replacement text shares a long accidental prefix/suffix with the original lands below the cut. The property that actually discriminates is SEMANTIC: does the pass construct the new block content INDEPENDENTLY of the old (whole-content replacement — e.g. launch-ack builds a fresh 3-line string, role-system sets '.', the TN branch builds a new wake-up string), or does it EXCISE a marker/chunk out of the surrounding text and keep the remainder (SR family, hook-prefix, git-lock, bd-noise, po-preview)?

So:
1. Determine the class per pass by READING each underlying strip function and recording the verdict with the source evidence (function + the line that sets the new content). That verdict is the classification.
2. Report the len(removed)/len(bt) DISTRIBUTION as corroborating evidence — per class, ideally showing whether the two classes actually separate. If they separate cleanly, say so and give the observed boundary as a MEASUREMENT. If they overlap, that overlap is itself a finding and must be reported, not smoothed away by picking a cut point.
3. No threshold anywhere in the classification logic. The blast-radius number ('full replacements currently recorded as a partial span, i.e. offset > 0 or suffix trimmed') is then counted within the semantically-determined FULL set.

Everything else stands. Go."

> - Korrektur an den Arbeiter geschickt, Freigabe für den Rest, Timer 10 Minuten läuft

**Der Arbeiter hat meine Vorgabe an einer Stelle verbessert und an einer verschlechtert.**
Verbessert: statt ganze Protokolldateien auszuschließen, filtert er nach der Struktur des Textes — nur was tatsächlich mit dem Meldungsanfang beginnt, zählt als Fundstelle. Damit fallen Quellcodezeilen und Berichtsausdrucke von selbst heraus, ohne dass echte Meldungen aus denselben Dateien mit verloren gehen. Das ist sauberer als mein Auftrag und bleibt.

**Verschlechtert: er wollte Voll- von Teilersetzung an einer willkürlichen Prozentschwelle unterscheiden.**
Sein Vorschlag war, alles über 85 Prozent entferntem Text als Vollersetzung zu zählen. Das misst aber nicht die Eigenschaft, auf die es ankommt. Eine echte Teilentfernung kann problemlos über 85 Prozent liegen, wenn der herausgeschnittene Block fast die ganze Nachricht ausmacht — und eine Vollersetzung kann darunter landen, wenn alter und neuer Text zufällig viel gemeinsam haben. Entscheidend ist nicht die Menge, sondern ob ein Durchlauf den neuen Inhalt unabhängig vom alten neu baut oder ob er ein Stück herausschneidet und den Rest stehen lässt. Das steht in der jeweiligen Funktion, ist also ablesbar statt schätzbar. Die Prozentzahlen soll er trotzdem erheben — als Gegenprobe, ob die beiden Klassen sich überhaupt trennen, und falls sie sich überlappen, ist genau das das Ergebnis.

**Ein Nebenbefund des Arbeiters ist ernst zu nehmen und geht in den Bericht.**
Bei dem Durchlauf, der einen Inhalt durch einen einzelnen Punkt ersetzt, wird dieser Punkt als gemeinsames Textende weggerechnet, wenn der Originaltext ebenfalls mit einem Punkt endet. Ergebnis wäre eine leere Ersetzungsspanne. Dieselbe Ursache wie bei unserem Fall, nur an einer anderen Stelle sichtbar.

**Belastbar ist damit schon jetzt: die manuelle Startform ist kein Einzelfall von heute Abend.**
Der Arbeiter hat sie in den Aufzeichnungen einer früheren Sitzung wörtlich gefunden, mit derselben Kennung über rund neunzig aufeinanderfolgende Protokollzeilen. Das ist die Bestätigung, die meiner eigenen Suche vorhin nicht gelungen war.

+    t = _ID_NORM_RE.sub('with ID: **<ID>**', text)

import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

_src_dir = os.path.join(os.environ.get("MONITOR_CC_ROOT", str(Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent)), "src")
sys.path.insert(0, _src_dir)

from .payload_helpers import _strip_blocked_tool_references  # re-exported for addon.py
from .content_strip import _strip_session_guidance, _strip_git_status
from .rules_config import _load_system2_rules
from .message_passes import (
    _apply_role_system_strip,
    _apply_sn_notice_strip,
    _apply_first_pass,
    _apply_cumulative_sr_strips,
    _apply_final_sr_pass,
    _apply_po_preview_strip,
    _apply_bg_exit_strip,
    _apply_bg_launch_ack_strip,
    _apply_hook_prefix_strip,
    _apply_git_lock_strip,
    _apply_bd_noise_strip,
    _dedup_wakeup_blocks,
)
from .rule_ops import _merge_ops

_WORKTREE_PATH_PATTERN = re.compile(r'(/[^\s]+)/\.claude/worktrees/[^/\s]+')

# Exact CC boilerplate text at system[1] — redundant once sys[2] (our injected rules) already
# establishes the agent's role. Exact-match guarded: an unexpected value at index 1 (future CC
# version changing this line) passes through untouched, never blindly nuked by index alone.
_SYS1_BOILERPLATE_TEXT = "You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude."

# ORCHESTRATOR

# Apply all proxy modification rules — returns (modified_payload, list_of_applied_rules, original_system2_text, stripped_msg_indices, stripped_msg_originals, stripped_msg_removed, injected_msg_added)
def apply_modification_rules(payload: dict, model_family: str = "opus", project_path: str = "") -> tuple:
    system_rules = _load_system2_rules(model_family, project_path)

    messages_to_process = list(payload.get("messages", []))
    modifications = []
    changed = False
    stripped_msg_indices = []
    stripped_msg_originals = {}
    stripped_msg_removed = {}
    injected_msg_added = {}
    _all_ops: dict = {}

    _passes = [
        _apply_role_system_strip,
        _apply_sn_notice_strip,
        _apply_first_pass,
        _apply_cumulative_sr_strips,
        _apply_final_sr_pass,
        _apply_po_preview_strip,
        _apply_bg_exit_strip,
        _apply_bg_launch_ack_strip,
        _apply_hook_prefix_strip,
        _apply_git_lock_strip,
        _apply_bd_noise_strip,
    ]

    new_messages = messages_to_process
    for pass_fn in _passes:
        new_messages, pass_mods, pass_removed, c_idxs, pass_injected, _pass_ops = pass_fn(new_messages)
        modifications.extend(pass_mods)
        for idx in c_idxs:
            if idx not in stripped_msg_indices:
                stripped_msg_indices.append(idx)
                stripped_msg_originals[idx] = messages_to_process[idx].get("content", "")
            stripped_msg_removed.setdefault(idx, []).extend(pass_removed.get(idx, []))
            injected_msg_added.setdefault(idx, []).extend(pass_injected.get(idx, []))
        if c_idxs:
            changed = True
        _merge_ops(_all_ops, _pass_ops)

    new_messages, _pass_ops = _dedup_wakeup_blocks(new_messages)
    _merge_ops(_all_ops, _pass_ops)

    new_system, original_system2_text, sys_mods, sys_changed = _apply_system_passes(
        payload.get("system", []), system_rules
    )
    modifications.extend(sys_mods)
    if sys_changed:
        changed = True

    if not changed:
        return payload, modifications, None, stripped_msg_indices, stripped_msg_originals, stripped_msg_removed, injected_msg_added, _all_ops

> - Diff geprüft: 4 neue Dateien, kein `src/` angetastet
> - D1-Bericht und Skript vollständig gelesen, D2-Bericht vollständig gelesen, Klassifikationslogik im D2-Skript geprüft
> - Eigene unabhängige Gegenprobe über denselben Korpus gefahren: 15 / 1, zwei Wortlaute — deckungsgleich
> - Suffix-Absorption von Hand nachgerechnet, Reihenfolge der Durchläufe in `rules.py` gegen die Skriptannahme geprüft
> - Drei Review-Notizen plus Recap-Auftrag geschickt

**Die Messung hält, und ich habe das Kernergebnis selbst nachgerechnet statt es zu übernehmen.**
Zwei Wortlaute, fünfzehn Vorkommen für den bekannten, eines für den manuell verschobenen — meine eigene Zählung kommt auf dieselben Zahlen. Damit ist bestätigt, was mir vorher nicht gelang: die zweite Form ist echt und keine Eigenart des heutigen Abends. Ein dritter Wortlaut existiert nicht. Der Arbeiter hat den Filter dabei absichtlich weiter gefasst, als die zwei bekannten Formen verlangen, damit eine unbekannte Variante aufgefallen wäre.

**Die Reichweite der Spannen-Änderung ist klein und liegt genau dort, wo sie hingehört.**
Von 140 aufgezeichneten Ersetzungen sind 97 Vollersetzungen, und nur 17 davon werden heute fälschlich als Teiländerung geführt — 15 aus der Startbestätigung, 2 aus dem Punkt-Ersatz. Alle 43 echten Teiländerungen bleiben unberührt. Die Änderung an der gemeinsamen Funktion ist damit verantwortbar.

**Die Prozentschwelle, die ich verworfen hatte, wäre tatsächlich falsch gewesen — und das ist jetzt gemessen, nicht behauptet.**
Die Wertebereiche beider Klassen überlappen: Vollersetzungen liegen zwischen 0,973 und 1,0, Teiländerungen zwischen 0,015 und 1,0. Es gibt also keinen Schnittpunkt, der die beiden trennt. Die Einordnung anhand der jeweiligen Funktion war die richtige Wahl.

**Drei Dinge habe ich beim Nachprüfen gefunden, die der Arbeiter zu optimistisch dargestellt hat.**
Erstens ist der Messkorpus während der Messung selbst gewachsen — der eine Bericht zählt 511 Anfragen, der andere 523, bei angeblich identischem Korpus. Eine der eingeschlossenen Dateien wuchs also weiter. Die Zahlen sind damit Untergrenzen auf einer bewegten Momentaufnahme; die Schlussfolgerung überlebt das, weil meine Gegenprobe auf dem gewachsenen Stand dieselben Werte liefert. Zweitens zeigt der Vorher-Nachher-Vergleich beim Punkt-Ersatz gar keinen Unterschied, weil der Unterschied ausschließlich in der Farbe liegt und der Bericht die Farbcodes entfernt — der Befund steht auf den Rohdaten, nicht auf dieser Darstellung. Drittens ist seine Erklärung, warum viele Durchläufe null Treffer haben, eine Hypothese: schlichtes Fehlen der Textmarken im Korpus würde dieselbe Null erzeugen. Alle drei gehen so in die Dokumentation.

176	+# Blast-radius measurement: full-replacement-aware `_extract_block_op`, 2026-07-29
177	+
178	+Milestone-1 measurement task: before any fix, quantify how many of the 17 real
179	+`_ops_from_content_change` call sites in `src/proxy/message_passes.py` a full-replacement-aware
180	+`_extract_block_op` (`src/proxy/rule_ops.py`) would actually change, and by how much. No
181	+production code touched. Script:
182	+`dev/proxy_instrumentation/p1_measure_full_replacement_blast_radius.py`.
183	+
184	+## Trigger
185	+
186	+`_extract_block_op(before, after)` reduces any content change to one `(offset, removed, injected)`
187	+op by walking off the common prefix/suffix. When a pass replaces a block's ENTIRE content and the
188	+replacement happens to share a leading word with the original — both the CC background-launch ack
189	+and the proxy's own replacement text start with `"Command"` — the recorded op starts mid-text.
190	+`_render_span_content` (`proxy_display/render_messages.py`) then emits the shared leading fragment
191	+unhighlighted on its own line and the rest green below: a 2-line split instead of one contiguous
192	+green block. `_extract_block_op` is reached from all 17 call sites via `_ops_from_content_change`
193	+(`message_passes.py`) — any change there affects every pass, not only the launch-ack one, which is
194	+the risk this measurement quantifies before touching the function.
195	+
196	+## Method — classification is semantic per call site, not a ratio threshold
197	+
198	+Each of the 17 call sites was classified by reading the underlying strip function: **FULL** = new
199	+block content is constructed independently of the old (a fixed literal, or a freshly-derived
200	+string, with no attempt to preserve surrounding text). **PARTIAL** = a known marker/chunk is
201	+excised from within the text (`regex.sub` / `str.replace` / slice) and everything else in the
202	+block is kept verbatim. **STRUCTURAL** = neither (an index-shift artifact from
203	+`_dedup_wakeup_blocks`'s list-branch dropping a duplicate block, not a designed content
204	+transform). A `len(removed)/len(bt)` ratio was computed per op as corroborating evidence only,
205	+never as the classifier — confirmed necessary: measured FULL ratios spanned [0.973, 1.000] and
206	+PARTIAL ratios spanned [0.015, 1.000] in the same corpus, an overlapping range that a fixed
207	+threshold would misclassify in both directions (a large SR block excised from a mostly-empty
208	+surrounding message scores near 1.0 despite being genuinely PARTIAL; `_apply_first_pass`'s TN
209	+branch scored exactly 1.0 for a message whose only content was the tag itself, despite being
210	+mechanistically PARTIAL — excise-and-keep-remainder, just with nothing left to keep in that
211	+instance).
212	+
213	+3 sites are FULL: `_apply_role_system_strip` (content set to literal `.`),
214	+`_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip` (block text wholesale-replaced by `_build_launch_ack_replacement`),
215	+`_apply_first_pass`'s rejection branch (`_strip_rejection_message` sets matched content to literal
216	+`.`). 13 sites are PARTIAL (all the SR-family passes, `_apply_first_pass`'s other 4 branches,
217	+`_apply_po_preview_strip`, `_apply_bg_exit_strip`, `_apply_hook_prefix_strip`,
218	+`_apply_git_lock_strip`, `_apply_bd_noise_strip`, `_dedup_wakeup_blocks`'s str-branch). 1 site
219	+(`_dedup_wakeup_blocks`'s list-branch) is STRUCTURAL — 0 occurrences in the measured corpus.
220	+
221	+`_apply_first_pass` is one function with 5 internal elif-branches carrying 3 different
222	+classifications; sub-classified per message by re-evaluating the same branch conditions the real
223	+function uses (`_top_level_content_contains`, `_message_has_rejection`, imported from their real
224	+modules, not reimplemented).
225	+
226	+## Findings (as of 2026-07-29, 522-523 requests scanned, 140 ops captured across all 17 sites)
227	+
228	+- FULL-class ops: 97 (82 `_apply_role_system_strip`, 15 `_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip`, 0
229	+  rejection-branch in this corpus). Of those, currently recorded as trimmed (`offset>0` or a
230	+  trimmed suffix — would render as a 2-piece split today, would become one contiguous span under a
231	+  full-replacement-aware op): **17** — all 15 `_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip` ops (100% of that site,
232	+  the flagship defect) + 2 `_apply_role_system_strip` ops (2.4% of that site).
233	+- 9 of the 17 call sites had 0 ops in this corpus (all 5 `_apply_first_pass` sub-branches except
234	+  TN, `_apply_cumulative_sr_strips`, `_apply_final_sr_pass`, `_apply_git_lock_strip`,
235	+  `_apply_bd_noise_strip`, `_dedup_wakeup_blocks` both branches) — stated plainly, not folded into
236	+  the observed-site table.
237	+
238	+**Hypothesis, not established fact, for the 0-op PARTIAL sites:** `_apply_role_system_strip` runs
239	+FIRST in the real pipeline and wholesale-replaces any role='system' message content (without a
240	+`<task-notification>` tag) with `.`. One candidate explanation for several PARTIAL sites' 0-op
241	+count is that their target markers (deferred-tools nag, task-tools nag, skills/agent-types/
242	+claudeMd SR blocks) arrived on role='system' messages in this corpus and were consumed wholesale
243	+by `_apply_role_system_strip` before the later, genuinely-PARTIAL passes ever saw them — one
244	+concrete render instance in the report is consistent with this (deferred-tools + agent-types +
245	+skills text arriving on a role='system' message, wholesale-`.`-replaced). This supports the
246	+hypothesis for that one instance; it does not establish the mechanism generally. An equally
247	+consistent alternative is plain absence of those markers on role='user' messages in this corpus,
248	+which would produce the identical 0-count with no upstream-consumption effect at all. Not
249	+distinguished — would require directly checking role='user' messages for these markers, out of
250	+scope for this measurement.
251	+
252	+## Flagged edge case — `.`-replacement absorbed as a common suffix
253	+
254	+For the 2 FULL sites whose replacement is the literal `.` (`_apply_role_system_strip`,
255	+`_apply_first_pass`'s rejection branch), when the ORIGINAL block text also happens to end in `.`,
256	+the single-char injected `.` gets absorbed entirely as the common suffix — the recorded op then has
257	+an EMPTY `injected` string. Confirmed directly against `_extract_block_op` (independent review,
258	+2026-07-29): `before='abc.', after='.'` → `offset=0, removed='abc', injected=''`. Measured: 2 of 82
259	+`_apply_role_system_strip` ops in this corpus hit this exact condition.
260	+
261	+The rendered before/after comparison in the report does NOT demonstrate this edge case visually —
262	+the absorbed `.` remains present in `compose_block`'s output as an unmodified `equal` span (same
263	+character position in both before/after), it does not disappear from the rendered text. What
264	+changes is only the span TAG on that character (`equal`/DIM today vs `injected`/green under a
265	+full-replacement-aware op) — an ANSI color/background attribute, not a text-content difference.
266	+After stripping ANSI codes for the markdown report, the two renders are textually near-identical.
267	+The finding rests on the op data alone (`injected == ''` vs the hypothetical `injected == '.'`),
268	+not on the rendered text — the bg-launch-ack case elsewhere in the same report IS a genuine
269	+visible text-split and is unaffected by this caveat.
270	+
271	+## Corpus was not static during measurement — op counts are a lower bound
272	+
273	+Request counts varied 519-523 across reruns of the same script within one measurement session, and
274	+diverged from a related same-day measurement's 511 on the nominally identical 4-file corpus —
275	+`opus_posts_1785338463` grew from 105 to 143 lines (mtime after both measurement runs) during/
276	+after the session. All op counts above are a lower bound on a moving snapshot, not a final static
277	+total. The qualitative findings (bg-launch-ack always FULL+trimmed; role_system_strip as the
278	+dominant FULL site; the semantic FULL/PARTIAL split; the ratio-range overlap) are not expected to
279	+change in kind under a rescan, only in magnitude.
280	+
281	+## Relevant Symbols / Paths
282	+
283	+- `_extract_block_op`, `_ops_from_content_change` (`src/proxy/rule_ops.py`) — function under
284	+  measurement
285	+- `compose_block` (`src/proxy/diff_engine.py`), `_render_span_content`
286	+  (`src/proxy_display/render_messages.py`) — real rendering pipeline reused (unmodified) to
287	+  produce the before/after comparisons
288	+- `dev/proxy_instrumentation/p1_measure_full_replacement_blast_radius.py` — measurement script,
289	+  re-runnable
290	+- `dev/proxy_instrumentation/md/full_replacement_blast_radius_20260729.md` — full report
291	+  (per-site evidence table, ratio distributions, 3 rendered before/after cases)
292	+- Corpus: `src/logs/dual_log/api_requests_{opus_monitor_cc_1785336796,opus_posts_1785338463,
293	+  opus_wise2627_1785324012,worker_25c51a2e_tn-role-system_1785344818}_original.jsonl`

+user manually backgrounds an already-running Bash call) that the proxy's `_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_PREFIX`
+anchor does not recognize at all — no replacement, original text forwarded verbatim. The 220-char
+live-observed text (id/path redacted): `Command was manually backgrounded by user with ID:
+<id>. Output is being written to: <path>` — notably missing the trailing `. You will be notified
+when it completes...` sentence the existing `_ACK_PATH_RE` uses as its terminator.
+
+## Corpus
+
+`src/logs/dual_log/*_original.jsonl`, 6 session files present at scan time. Included 4: two prior
+completed Opus sessions (`opus_monitor_cc_1785336796`, `opus_posts_1785338463`), one long Opus
+session (`opus_wise2627_1785324012`), one prior worker session (`worker_..._tn-role-system_
+1785344818`). Excluded 2: the currently-live orchestrating Opus session
+(`opus_monitor_cc_1785347492`, still growing at scan time) and this worker's own worktree activity
+(`worker_..._bg-ack-shapes_1785359201`, proxy log starting at dispatch time) — both would let the
+measurement's own tool calls masquerade as corpus evidence.
+
+**Contamination beyond file-level exclusion:** `opus_posts` and `tn-role-system` are themselves
+prior investigative sessions on this exact defect area. Raw substring grep for `"Output is being
+written to:"` hit not just genuine acks but source lines (`_ACK_PATH_RE = re.compile(...)`),
+templated dev-report printouts (`${O}`, `<pfad>`, `#3: '...'`), and Read-tool dumps of
+`strip_bg_launch_ack.py` — reappearing in every later cumulative dual-log snapshot of that session.
+Blanket-excluding those files would also discard genuine acks the same sessions produced by
+actually running real background Bash calls. Resolved with a structural filter instead of file
+exclusion: a candidate is only counted if the JSON-parsed block's FULL text starts with `Command`
+at position 0 — Read-tool dumps start with line numbers, docstrings start with other prose, report
+printouts start with `===`/`#N:`, none of them satisfy a block-initial match.
+
+**Dedup:** dual-log lines are cumulative snapshots of the whole conversation so far; a message once
+introduced reappears verbatim in every later request of its session. Deduped via a
+prev-message-count delta (only `messages[prev_count:]` inspected per request) rather than raw
+substring counting. Demonstrated concretely: one genuine occurrence (same `toolu_id`, same text)
+appeared raw 1014 times across the cumulative snapshots of `opus_monitor_cc_1785336796` alone;
+deduped, that session contributed 16 genuine occurrences total.
+
+## Findings (as of 2026-07-29, 511 requests scanned across the 4 included sessions)
+
+Exactly 2 distinct wordings found, no others, despite the structural filter being deliberately
+broad (`Command` + `with ID:` + `Output is being written to:`, not hardcoded to either exact known
+wording):
+
+1. `Command running in background with ID: <id>. Output is being written to: <path>. You will be
+   notified when it completes. To check interim output, use Read on that file path.` — 15 deduped
+   occurrences, 2 of 4 sessions, role=user, shape=tool_result_str. All 3 mechanisms fire correctly
+   (`_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_MARKER` fires, `_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_PREFIX` fires, both regexes extract).
+2. `Command was manually backgrounded by user with ID: <id>. Output is being written to: <path>` —
+   1 deduped occurrence, 1 of 4 sessions, role=user, shape=tool_result_str. Matches the live-
+   observed text's template exactly. ALL 3 mechanisms fail: it does not contain `"running in
+   background with ID"` so the fast-path gate never even reaches the replacement walker; the
+   prefix startswith check fails (`"Command was manually"` ≠ `"Command running"`); both regexes
+   fail to extract (anchored on the wrong literal prefix).
+
+No third wording found. A long-running Bash call WITHOUT `run_in_background` is killed on timeout
+(exit 143), not backgrounded, per a separate live observation the same day — consistent with
+finding no third launch-wording family in the corpus.

+# Blast-radius measurement: full-replacement-aware `_extract_block_op`, 2026-07-29
+
+Milestone-1 measurement task: before any fix, quantify how many of the 17 real
+`_ops_from_content_change` call sites in `src/proxy/message_passes.py` a full-replacement-aware
+`_extract_block_op` (`src/proxy/rule_ops.py`) would actually change, and by how much. No
+production code touched. Script:
+`dev/proxy_instrumentation/p1_measure_full_replacement_blast_radius.py`.
+
+## Trigger
+
+`_extract_block_op(before, after)` reduces any content change to one `(offset, removed, injected)`
+op by walking off the common prefix/suffix. When a pass replaces a block's ENTIRE content and the
+replacement happens to share a leading word with the original — both the CC background-launch ack
+and the proxy's own replacement text start with `"Command"` — the recorded op starts mid-text.
+`_render_span_content` (`proxy_display/render_messages.py`) then emits the shared leading fragment
+unhighlighted on its own line and the rest green below: a 2-line split instead of one contiguous
+green block. `_extract_block_op` is reached from all 17 call sites via `_ops_from_content_change`
+(`message_passes.py`) — any change there affects every pass, not only the launch-ack one, which is
+the risk this measurement quantifies before touching the function.
+
+## Method — classification is semantic per call site, not a ratio threshold
+
+Each of the 17 call sites was classified by reading the underlying strip function: **FULL** = new
+block content is constructed independently of the old (a fixed literal, or a freshly-derived
+string, with no attempt to preserve surrounding text). **PARTIAL** = a known marker/chunk is
+excised from within the text (`regex.sub` / `str.replace` / slice) and everything else in the
+block is kept verbatim. **STRUCTURAL** = neither (an index-shift artifact from
+`_dedup_wakeup_blocks`'s list-branch dropping a duplicate block, not a designed content
+transform). A `len(removed)/len(bt)` ratio was computed per op as corroborating evidence only,
+never as the classifier — confirmed necessary: measured FULL ratios spanned [0.973, 1.000] and
+PARTIAL ratios spanned [0.015, 1.000] in the same corpus, an overlapping range that a fixed
+threshold would misclassify in both directions (a large SR block excised from a mostly-empty
+surrounding message scores near 1.0 despite being genuinely PARTIAL; `_apply_first_pass`'s TN
+branch scored exactly 1.0 for a message whose only content was the tag itself, despite being
+mechanistically PARTIAL — excise-and-keep-remainder, just with nothing left to keep in that
+instance).
+
+3 sites are FULL: `_apply_role_system_strip` (content set to literal `.`),
+`_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip` (block text wholesale-replaced by `_build_launch_ack_replacement`),
+`_apply_first_pass`'s rejection branch (`_strip_rejection_message` sets matched content to literal
+`.`). 13 sites are PARTIAL (all the SR-family passes, `_apply_first_pass`'s other 4 branches,
+`_apply_po_preview_strip`, `_apply_bg_exit_strip`, `_apply_hook_prefix_strip`,
+`_apply_git_lock_strip`, `_apply_bd_noise_strip`, `_dedup_wakeup_blocks`'s str-branch). 1 site
+(`_dedup_wakeup_blocks`'s list-branch) is STRUCTURAL — 0 occurrences in the measured corpus.
+
+`_apply_first_pass` is one function with 5 internal elif-branches carrying 3 different
+classifications; sub-classified per message by re-evaluating the same branch conditions the real
+function uses (`_top_level_content_contains`, `_message_has_rejection`, imported from their real
+modules, not reimplemented).
+
+## Findings (as of 2026-07-29, 522-523 requests scanned, 140 ops captured across all 17 sites)
+
+- FULL-class ops: 97 (82 `_apply_role_system_strip`, 15 `_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip`, 0
+  rejection-branch in this corpus). Of those, currently recorded as trimmed (`offset>0` or a
+  trimmed suffix — would render as a 2-piece split today, would become one contiguous span under a
+  full-replacement-aware op): **17** — all 15 `_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip` ops (100% of that site,
+  the flagship defect) + 2 `_apply_role_system_strip` ops (2.4% of that site).
+- 9 of the 17 call sites had 0 ops in this corpus (all 5 `_apply_first_pass` sub-branches except
+  TN, `_apply_cumulative_sr_strips`, `_apply_final_sr_pass`, `_apply_git_lock_strip`,
+  `_apply_bd_noise_strip`, `_dedup_wakeup_blocks` both branches) — stated plainly, not folded into
+  the observed-site table.
+
+**Hypothesis, not established fact, for the 0-op PARTIAL sites:** `_apply_role_system_strip` runs
+FIRST in the real pipeline and wholesale-replaces any role='system' message content (without a
+`<task-notification>` tag) with `.`. One candidate explanation for several PARTIAL sites' 0-op
+count is that their target markers (deferred-tools nag, task-tools nag, skills/agent-types/
+claudeMd SR blocks) arrived on role='system' messages in this corpus and were consumed wholesale
+by `_apply_role_system_strip` before the later, genuinely-PARTIAL passes ever saw them — one
+concrete render instance in the report is consistent with this (deferred-tools + agent-types +
+skills text arriving on a role='system' message, wholesale-`.`-replaced). This supports the
+hypothesis for that one instance; it does not establish the mechanism generally. An equally
+consistent alternative is plain absence of those markers on role='user' messages in this corpus,
+which would produce the identical 0-count with no upstream-consumption effect at all. Not
+distinguished — would require directly checking role='user' messages for these markers, out of
+scope for this measurement.
+
+## Flagged edge case — `.`-replacement absorbed as a common suffix
+
+For the 2 FULL sites whose replacement is the literal `.` (`_apply_role_system_strip`,
+`_apply_first_pass`'s rejection branch), when the ORIGINAL block text also happens to end in `.`,
+the single-char injected `.` gets absorbed entirely as the common suffix — the recorded op then has
+an EMPTY `injected` string. Confirmed directly against `_extract_block_op` (independent review,
+2026-07-29): `before='abc.', after='.'` → `offset=0, removed='abc', injected=''`. Measured: 2 of 82
+`_apply_role_system_strip` ops in this corpus hit this exact condition.
+
+The rendered before/after comparison in the report does NOT demonstrate this edge case visually —
+the absorbed `.` remains present in `compose_block`'s output as an unmodified `equal` span (same
+character position in both before/after), it does not disappear from the rendered text. What
+changes is only the span TAG on that character (`equal`/DIM today vs `injected`/green under a
+full-replacement-aware op) — an ANSI color/background attribute, not a text-content difference.
+After stripping ANSI codes for the markdown report, the two renders are textually near-identical.
+The finding rests on the op data alone (`injected == ''` vs the hypothetical `injected == '.'`),
+not on the rendered text — the bg-launch-ack case elsewhere in the same report IS a genuine
+visible text-split and is unaffected by this caveat.
+
+## Corpus was not static during measurement — op counts are a lower bound
+
+Request counts varied 519-523 across reruns of the same script within one measurement session, and
+diverged from a related same-day measurement's 511 on the nominally identical 4-file corpus —
+`opus_posts_1785338463` grew from 105 to 143 lines (mtime after both measurement runs) during/
+after the session. All op counts above are a lower bound on a moving snapshot, not a final static
+total. The qualitative findings (bg-launch-ack always FULL+trimmed; role_system_strip as the
+dominant FULL site; the semantic FULL/PARTIAL split; the ratio-range overlap) are not expected to
+change in kind under a rescan, only in magnitude.
+
+## Relevant Symbols / Paths
+
+- `_extract_block_op`, `_ops_from_content_change` (`src/proxy/rule_ops.py`) — function under
+  measurement
+- `compose_block` (`src/proxy/diff_engine.py`), `_render_span_content`
+  (`src/proxy_display/render_messages.py`) — real rendering pipeline reused (unmodified) to
+  produce the before/after comparisons
+- `dev/proxy_instrumentation/p1_measure_full_replacement_blast_radius.py` — measurement script,
+  re-runnable
+- `dev/proxy_instrumentation/md/full_replacement_blast_radius_20260729.md` — full report
+  (per-site evidence table, ratio distributions, 3 rendered before/after cases)
+- Corpus: `src/logs/dual_log/api_requests_{opus_monitor_cc_1785336796,opus_posts_1785338463,
+  opus_wise2627_1785324012,worker_25c51a2e_tn-role-system_1785344818}_original.jsonl`

# Milestone 2 — recognize the SECOND CC launch-ack wording

FIRST: in your worktree run `git fetch origin integration && git merge integration`, verify it merged cleanly, THEN do the task below.

## Task

Your own M1 measurement established: exactly 2 distinct CC background-launch-ack wordings exist in the recorded corpus, and wording 2 fails ALL THREE recognition mechanisms in `src/proxy/strip_bg_launch_ack.py`. Make the proxy handle wording 2 exactly as it handles wording 1 — the same 3-line replacement (message / `Output: <path>` / `ID: <id>`), with the path line present.

Your M1 report `dev/bg_wakeup_id_line/md/launch_ack_wordings_20260729.md` holds the verbatim texts and the per-mechanism fire/no-fire matrix. Use it as the spec.

Files in scope (starting set, not a fence):
- `src/proxy/strip_bg_launch_ack.py` — the marker, the anchored prefix check, the id/path extraction, the replacement builder
- `src/proxy/message_passes.py::_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip` — the fast-path gate that currently skips wording-2 messages entirely
- `src/proxy/strip_vocab.py` — the `BL` attribution entry keys on the same literal; a second wording must not produce a wrong or missing pane attribution
- `dev/proxy/test_strip_fix.py`, `dev/proxy_dual_log/proxy_176_bg_launch_ack_tests.py`, `dev/proxy/proxy_bgcomplete_tests.py` — existing suites

- wording 2 has no `. You will be notified when it completes...` trailing sentence — the current `_ACK_PATH_RE` terminates on exactly that literal, so it cannot extract wording 2's path
- wording 2's text is the complete block (ends after the path)

- BOTH wordings produce the same canonical 3-line output shape, path line included
- the FP-nuke guard stays intact: a large tool_result or user message that merely CONTAINS an ack phrase as quoted data must never be replaced. This anchored-match property is load-bearing (it was a real past bug in this repo) — it must hold for the new wording exactly as for the old.
- missing-value behavior unchanged: a value that fails to extract is OMITTED, never `ID: None`, never a dangling label

## Constraints

- Scope is exactly the above. Do NOT fix `_extract_block_op` / the span-trim defect — that is milestone 3, a different file, deliberately separate.
- Do NOT add features, refactors, or improvements beyond this deliverable.
- Do NOT search externally (no web, no RAG, no gh). If you hit a genuine external need, STOP and ask.
- Commit in your worktree.

Report your approach and anything your reading contradicts. - [ ] Pane attribution (`strip_vocab.py` BL) verified to resolve for wording 2 — state how you verified
- [ ] Exact commands run, with results

Tatsächlich lag der Grenzfall anders: ein Durchlauf schneidet ein Stück heraus und behält den Rest — nur war in dem gemessenen Fall gar kein Rest übrig, weshalb der Wert bei 1,0 landet, obwohl der Mechanismus ein Herausschneiden ist. Der Unterschied ist wichtig, weil er zeigt, dass die Prozentzahl den Mechanismus grundsätzlich nicht abbildet.

**Meilenstein 2 läuft jetzt: die zweite Startform erkennen.**
Ich habe dem Arbeiter zwei Entscheidungen ausdrücklich offengelassen und deren Begründung eingefordert — ob die Pfaderkennung mit einem oder zwei Ausdrücken arbeitet, und ob die Vorfilterung zwei Textmarken trägt oder eine breitere. Die zweite Wahl hat eine Nebenwirkung: eine breitere Marke greift auch bei zitierten Texten häufiger, und genau davor schützt die Verankerung am Textanfang. Diese Schutzeigenschaft ist in diesem Projekt schon einmal gebrochen worden, deshalb steht sie im Auftrag als unverhandelbar.

Gemessen: hängt man an die Meldung eine weitere Zeile an, steht diese Zeile mit im Pfad. Ich habe ihm die Richtung der Reparatur vorgegeben, am Zeilenende statt am Textende abzuschneiden, und eine Prüfung genau für diese Form verlangt.

> - Produktivcode-Diff vollständig gelesen: fünf Dateien, davon drei im Produktivcode, alle Änderungen im vereinbarten Rahmen
> - Beide Ausdrücke selbst gegen sieben Grenzfälle nachgerechnet
> - Alle drei Prüfsammlungen selbst gefahren: 126 von 126, 42 von 42, 33 von 33, jeweils null Fehlschläge
> - FP-Schutztest im Diff gelesen und auf die richtigen vier Zusicherungen geprüft
> - Recap für Meilenstein 2 ausgelöst, Timer 10 Minuten

**Die Korrektur sitzt, und der von mir gemeldete Grenzfall ist jetzt sowohl behoben als auch festgenagelt.**
Der Pfad-Ausdruck endet nun am Zeilenende statt am Textende. Ich habe das nicht dem Bericht des Arbeiters entnommen, sondern selbst durchgerechnet: hängt man Folgetext an die Meldung, bleibt der Pfad sauber. Die erste Form liefert dabei byte-gleich dasselbe wie vorher, auch mit einem Zeilenumbruch mitten im Text.

**Ein achter Fall, den ich zusätzlich probiert habe, verhält sich richtig.**
Eine Meldung ohne Pfadangabe überhaupt liefert nur die Kennung, und die Pfadzeile entfällt — kein leeres Etikett, kein Müllpfad. Das ist genau die Zusicherung, die in der ursprünglichen Fassung als Schutz gegen fehlende Werte gebaut wurde, und sie hält für die neue Form ebenso.

**Der Schutz gegen versehentliches Löschen zitierter Texte ist unangetastet geblieben — nachgeprüft, nicht geglaubt.**
Der neue Prüffall stellt eine Nachricht her, die den neuen Wortlaut mitten im Inhalt zitiert, und stellt vier Dinge fest: Inhalt unverändert, keine Änderungsmeldung, kein Eintrag in der Änderungsliste, nichts entfernt. Genau diese Eigenschaft war in diesem Projekt früher einmal gebrochen.

**Was noch offen bleibt: der Live-Beweis am neu gestarteten Proxy.**
Der laufende Proxy arbeitet mit einer eingefrorenen Kopie des Codes und übernimmt die Änderung erst nach einem Neustart. Der endgültige Nachweis ist also derselbe Versuch wie heute Abend — ein Aufruf, den du manuell in den Hintergrund schiebst — nur nach dem Neustart. Den brauche ich von dir, und zwar erst nach Meilenstein 3, damit ein Neustart beide Reparaturen auf einmal aufnimmt.
