7	+# Recognizing the second CC background-launch-ack wording, 2026-07-29
8	+
9	+Milestone-2 fix: the M1 wording inventory (2026-07-29, same area) established exactly 2 distinct
10	+CC background-launch-ack wordings in the recorded corpus and that wording 2 failed all 3
11	+recognition mechanisms in `strip_bg_launch_ack.py`. This entry records the fix and the reasoning
12	+behind each design choice, not just the diff.
13	+
14	+## The two wordings
15	+
16	+- Wording 1 (initial background launch): `"Command running in background with ID: <id>. Output
17	+  is being written to: <path>. You will be notified when it completes. To check interim output,
18	+  use Read on that file path."`
19	+- Wording 2 (user manually backgrounds an already-running Bash call): `"Command was manually
20	+  backgrounded by user with ID: <id>. Output is being written to: <path>"` — no trailing sentence;
21	+  the ack was the complete block in the only measured corpus occurrence.
22	+
23	+Both produce the identical 3-line replacement shape (hold-instruction line, then optional
24	+`Output: <path>`, then optional `ID: <id>`) — the hold-instruction line itself is byte-identical
25	+regardless of which wording matched; only the recovered id/path differ.
26	+
27	+## Design choice — two narrow markers/prefixes, OR'd, not one broadened marker
28	+
29	+The fast-path gate (`message_passes.py`) and the anchored decision (`strip_bg_launch_ack.py`)
30	+each gained a second constant (`_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_MARKER_2`, `_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_PREFIX_2`) checked via
31	+OR, rather than widening the existing single marker/prefix to a shared broad substring (e.g. a
32	+bare `"with ID:"`). Reasoning: a broadened marker would match arbitrary unrelated text quoting an
33	+id anywhere and reopen exactly the false-positive-nuke class of bug the anchored-match design
34	+already exists to prevent in this file (a real past bug in this repo, per the module's own
35	+comments) — a large tool_result or pasted user message merely containing an ack-like phrase as
36	+quoted data must never be replaced. Two markers, each staying exactly as narrow/specific to its
37	+own wording as the original single marker was, preserve that precision for both wordings
38	+independently instead of trading it away for code brevity.
39	+
40	+## Why loosening the ID/PATH extraction regexes is FP-safe, but the prefix check is not touched
41	+
42	+`_ACK_ID_RE` was loosened from anchoring on the full wording-1 sentence prefix to anchoring on
43	+just the `"with ID:"` fragment common to both wordings — this is safe ONLY because `_ACK_ID_RE`
44	+and `_ACK_PATH_RE` are exclusively reachable from `_build_launch_ack_replacement`, and every call
45	+site of that function is gated behind a prior `_is_bg_launch_ack(text)` check on the SAME text
46	+(confirmed by reading every call site in `_strip_bg_launch_ack`). By the time either regex runs,
47	+the text is already confirmed a genuine, block-initial-anchored ack — the false-positive surface
48	+lives entirely in `_is_bg_launch_ack`'s `startswith` check, not in what happens to the text
49	+afterward. This is why `_is_bg_launch_ack` was NOT simplified the same way (e.g. to a shared
50	+`"Command"` + `"with ID:"` combination) — that check is the load-bearing FP guard and stays two
51	+full, wording-specific literal prefixes, each as strict as before.
52	+
53	+## One alternation regex, not two wording-specific regexes, for both ID and path
54	+
55	+Both wordings share the literal `"with ID: <id>."` and `"Output is being written to:"` substrings
56	+verbatim — only wording 2 lacks the wording-1 trailing sentence that the original `_ACK_PATH_RE`
57	+used as its sole terminator. A single regex with an alternation-based terminator (wording-1's
58	+`". You will be notified"` sentence, OR a line boundary, tried in that order) lets
59	+`_build_launch_ack_replacement` stay completely wording-agnostic — it has no branch on which
60	+wording matched, it just calls `.search()` once per field, exactly as before. Splitting into two
61	+parallel wording-specific regexes would have required threading "which wording matched" through
62	+the call, for no benefit given the two wordings' shared substrings.
63	+
64	+## The path-regex newline bound — a real failure mode, not hypothetical
65	+
66	+The first version of the path-regex fix used `\s*$` (end-of-string) as the fallback terminator for
67	+wording 2 (which lacks the trailing sentence). Hand-verification before implementing surfaced a
68	+real swallowing failure mode with `re.DOTALL` enabled: a wording-2 ack followed by ANY trailing
69	+content in the same block (e.g. `"<wording-2 ack>\nsome trailing note"`) had that trailing content
70	+swallowed whole into the `Output:` line's path capture — the ID line stayed correct, but the
71	+Output line became `path + "\n" + trailing text` instead of just the path. This is not a
72	+constructed hypothetical: the M1 blast-radius classification of this exact pass (measured
73	+separately, same area) already establishes that `_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip` discards "ANY
74	+trailing content after the ack in that block" as part of its own replacement mechanism — a block
75	+with trailing content after the ack is a shape the pass already contemplates, simply unobserved in
76	+the specific corpus snapshot measured for the wording inventory (the one real wording-2 occurrence
77	+happened to BE the entire block). Fixed by adding a literal `\n` as an earlier-tried alternative
78	+in the terminator alternation, bounding the fallback capture to the current LINE rather than the
79	+whole remaining string — `re.DOTALL` itself was kept (removing it wholesale was explicitly
80	+avoided, since the wording-1 branch relies on it to let the path capture cross a hypothetical
81	+internal newline before the real terminator sentence, though this is not exercised by any measured
82	+wording-1 occurrence either). Pinned as a regression guard: real ack text + a trailing line in the
83	+same block → the Output line carries only the path, the trailing text is absent from the entire
84	+replacement, the ID line is unaffected.
85	+

89	+`_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip`, `attribute_chunk`) called directly against the exact 220-char

94	+the ack phrase as quoted/pasted data, not block-initial, confirmed unchanged. NOT verified against
95	+a restarted live proxy with a genuine CC session where the user actually backgrounds an

+# Recognizing the second CC background-launch-ack wording, 2026-07-29
+
+Milestone-2 fix: the M1 wording inventory (2026-07-29, same area) established exactly 2 distinct
+CC background-launch-ack wordings in the recorded corpus and that wording 2 failed all 3
+recognition mechanisms in `strip_bg_launch_ack.py`. This entry records the fix and the reasoning
+behind each design choice, not just the diff.
+
+## The two wordings
+
+- Wording 1 (initial background launch): `"Command running in background with ID: <id>. Output
+  is being written to: <path>. You will be notified when it completes. To check interim output,
+  use Read on that file path."`
+- Wording 2 (user manually backgrounds an already-running Bash call): `"Command was manually
+  backgrounded by user with ID: <id>. Output is being written to: <path>"` — no trailing sentence;
+  the ack was the complete block in the only measured corpus occurrence.
+
+Both produce the identical 3-line replacement shape (hold-instruction line, then optional
+`Output: <path>`, then optional `ID: <id>`) — the hold-instruction line itself is byte-identical
+regardless of which wording matched; only the recovered id/path differ.
+
+## Design choice — two narrow markers/prefixes, OR'd, not one broadened marker
+
+The fast-path gate (`message_passes.py`) and the anchored decision (`strip_bg_launch_ack.py`)
+each gained a second constant (`_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_MARKER_2`, `_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_PREFIX_2`) checked via
+OR, rather than widening the existing single marker/prefix to a shared broad substring (e.g. a
+bare `"with ID:"`). Reasoning: a broadened marker would match arbitrary unrelated text quoting an
+id anywhere and reopen exactly the false-positive-nuke class of bug the anchored-match design
+already exists to prevent in this file (a real past bug in this repo, per the module's own
+comments) — a large tool_result or pasted user message merely containing an ack-like phrase as
+quoted data must never be replaced. Two markers, each staying exactly as narrow/specific to its
+own wording as the original single marker was, preserve that precision for both wordings
+independently instead of trading it away for code brevity.
+
+## Why loosening the ID/PATH extraction regexes is FP-safe, but the prefix check is not touched
+
+`_ACK_ID_RE` was loosened from anchoring on the full wording-1 sentence prefix to anchoring on
+just the `"with ID:"` fragment common to both wordings — this is safe ONLY because `_ACK_ID_RE`
+and `_ACK_PATH_RE` are exclusively reachable from `_build_launch_ack_replacement`, and every call
+site of that function is gated behind a prior `_is_bg_launch_ack(text)` check on the SAME text
+(confirmed by reading every call site in `_strip_bg_launch_ack`). By the time either regex runs,
+the text is already confirmed a genuine, block-initial-anchored ack — the false-positive surface
+lives entirely in `_is_bg_launch_ack`'s `startswith` check, not in what happens to the text
+afterward. This is why `_is_bg_launch_ack` was NOT simplified the same way (e.g. to a shared
+`"Command"` + `"with ID:"` combination) — that check is the load-bearing FP guard and stays two
+full, wording-specific literal prefixes, each as strict as before.
+
+## One alternation regex, not two wording-specific regexes, for both ID and path
+
+Both wordings share the literal `"with ID: <id>."` and `"Output is being written to:"` substrings
+verbatim — only wording 2 lacks the wording-1 trailing sentence that the original `_ACK_PATH_RE`
+used as its sole terminator. A single regex with an alternation-based terminator (wording-1's
+`". You will be notified"` sentence, OR a line boundary, tried in that order) lets
+`_build_launch_ack_replacement` stay completely wording-agnostic — it has no branch on which
+wording matched, it just calls `.search()` once per field, exactly as before. Splitting into two
+parallel wording-specific regexes would have required threading "which wording matched" through
+the call, for no benefit given the two wordings' shared substrings.
+
+## The path-regex newline bound — a real failure mode, not hypothetical
+
+The first version of the path-regex fix used `\s*$` (end-of-string) as the fallback terminator for
+wording 2 (which lacks the trailing sentence). Hand-verification before implementing surfaced a
+real swallowing failure mode with `re.DOTALL` enabled: a wording-2 ack followed by ANY trailing
+content in the same block (e.g. `"<wording-2 ack>\nsome trailing note"`) had that trailing content
+swallowed whole into the `Output:` line's path capture — the ID line stayed correct, but the
+Output line became `path + "\n" + trailing text` instead of just the path. This is not a
+constructed hypothetical: the M1 blast-radius classification of this exact pass (measured
+separately, same area) already establishes that `_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip` discards "ANY
+trailing content after the ack in that block" as part of its own replacement mechanism — a block
+with trailing content after the ack is a shape the pass already contemplates, simply unobserved in
+the specific corpus snapshot measured for the wording inventory (the one real wording-2 occurrence
+happened to BE the entire block). Fixed by adding a literal `\n` as an earlier-tried alternative
+in the terminator alternation, bounding the fallback capture to the current LINE rather than the
+whole remaining string — `re.DOTALL` itself was kept (removing it wholesale was explicitly
+avoided, since the wording-1 branch relies on it to let the path capture cross a hypothetical
+internal newline before the real terminator sentence, though this is not exercised by any measured
+wording-1 occurrence either). Pinned as a regression guard: real ack text + a trailing line in the
+same block → the Output line carries only the path, the trailing text is absent from the entire
+replacement, the ID line is unaffected.
+
+## Verification boundary (as of 2026-07-29)
+
+Verified at integration level: real production functions (`_strip_bg_launch_ack`,
+`_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip`, `attribute_chunk`) called directly against the exact 220-char
+live-observed wording-2 text, a real wording-1 corpus body (pre-existing exact-match regression
+guard, confirmed byte-identical output before vs after this change), and a synthetic
+trailing-content fixture exercising the newline-bound fix. The false-positive guard was verified
+the same way both wordings were verified for wording 1 originally — a message merely containing
+the ack phrase as quoted/pasted data, not block-initial, confirmed unchanged. NOT verified against
+a restarted live proxy with a genuine CC session where the user actually backgrounds an
+already-running Bash call — the running proxy uses a frozen source copy and only picks up a source
+change after restart; that gate is still open.
+
+## Relevant Symbols / Paths
+
+- `_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_MARKER`, `_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_MARKER_2`, `_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_PREFIX`,
+  `_BG_LAUNCH_ACK_PREFIX_2`, `_is_bg_launch_ack`, `_ACK_ID_RE`, `_ACK_PATH_RE`
+  (`src/proxy/strip_bg_launch_ack.py`)
+- `_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip`'s fast-path gate (`src/proxy/message_passes.py`)
+- `RULES['BL']` marker list (`src/proxy/strip_vocab.py`)
+- Regression guards: `W23`/`W24` (`dev/proxy/test_strip_fix.py`), Items 4m-4p
+  (`dev/proxy_dual_log/proxy_176_bg_launch_ack_tests.py`)
+- Corpus / live observation: `dev/bg_wakeup_id_line/md/launch_ack_wordings_20260729.md`

FIRST: in your worktree run `git fetch origin integration && git merge integration`, verify it merged cleanly, THEN do the task below.

## Task

Make `_extract_block_op` in `src/proxy/rule_ops.py` record a WHOLE-CONTENT replacement as ONE contiguous span, instead of trimming the common prefix/suffix and thereby recording it as a partial span.

Your own M1 blast-radius measurement (`dev/proxy_instrumentation/md/full_replacement_blast_radius_20260729.md`, `process-docs/proxy_instrumentation/2026-07-29_full_replacement_blast_radius_measurement.md`) is the spec and the risk budget for this change. It established, as of 2026-07-29:

- 17 call sites reach `_extract_block_op` via `_ops_from_content_change`; a change here affects ALL of them
- FULL-class ops: 97, of which 17 are today recorded as trimmed → these are the ones whose rendering changes
- PARTIAL-class ops: 43 — prefix/suffix trimming is CORRECT and DESIRABLE for these and must keep working exactly as today
- the FULL/PARTIAL ratio ranges OVERLAP ([0.973, 1.000] vs [0.015, 1.000]) — a size/ratio heuristic cannot discriminate the two classes, so do NOT introduce one
- flagged edge case: for a `.`-literal replacement whose original also ends in `.`, the injected `.` is absorbed as common suffix → `injected == ''` (2 of 82 `_apply_role_system_strip` ops). Confirmed independently: `before='abc.', after='.'` → `offset=0, removed='abc', injected=''`

- `src/proxy/rule_ops.py` — `_extract_block_op`, `_ops_from_content_change`
- `src/proxy/diff_engine.py::compose_block` / `apply_edit_to_spans` — consumes the ops

- your two M1 measurement scripts — re-runnable, and the natural before/after harness

- PARTIAL ops keep their current trimmed offsets/spans, byte-identical. This is the regression risk of the whole milestone; pin it.
- No ratio/size/length threshold anywhere in the decision.
- The composition invariant that `test_composition_invariant.py` guards must still hold.

- Do NOT add features, refactors, or improvements beyond this deliverable.
- Do NOT search externally (no web, no RAG, no gh). If you hit a genuine external need, STOP and ask.

Report your approach and anything your reading contradicts. Specifically:

Note that `_extract_block_op` only receives two strings — it has no knowledge of which pass called it. State plainly whether you can decide it from the two strings alone, or whether the caller must pass that knowledge in, and what that means for the 17 call sites.

=== msg 1/1 ===
## Investigation complete — report before implementing

### 1. How the "whole-content replacement" decision is made

`_extract_block_op(before, after)` receives only two strings — it **cannot** decide this from the strings alone without a ratio/size heuristic, which is explicitly forbidden (and M1 proved the FULL/PARTIAL ratio ranges overlap, so no threshold would work anyway). The decision must be an explicit flag passed in by the **caller**, because only the caller (the pass function) knows whether it constructs new content independently of the old, or excises a chunk from within surrounding text — exactly the semantic classification M1 already did by reading each pass function.

Plan: add `full_replace: bool = False` to both `_extract_block_op` and `_ops_from_content_change` (default preserves current behavior for every existing caller with zero code changes needed at those call sites — confirmed via grep: 3 dev/ test files call `_ops_from_content_change` directly with 2 positional args, all continue to get the old trimmed behavior unchanged). Of the 17 `message_passes.py` call sites, exactly **3** get `full_replace=True` (matching M1's FULL classification exactly): `_apply_role_system_strip` (line 70), `_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip` (line 466), and `_apply_first_pass`'s rejection branch specifically (line 240 — the other 4 branches of that same function, at lines 197/207/217/230, stay `False`). The other 14 call sites are untouched, byte-for-byte.

When `full_replace=True`: skip the prefix/suffix walk entirely, return `[(0, before, after)]`. I traced this through `compose_block`/`apply_edit_to_spans` by hand: with this op, the single `('equal', c0_text)` starting span splits into exactly one `('stripped', full_before)` + one `('injected', full_after)` — already renders as one contiguous green block via the **existing**, unmodified `_render_span_content`. No changes needed to `diff_engine.py` or `render_messages.py` at all.

Safety for list-content messages (bg_launch_ack, rejection-branch list case): `_ops_from_content_change`'s list branch calls `_extract_block_op(bt, at, full_replace)` per block index; for every block the pass left untouched, `bt == at` and the function returns `[]` on its very first line — before `full_replace` is even consulted. > - Heutigen Zuschnitt gegengerechnet: liefert genau die live beobachtete Zweiteilung

**Der Entwurf ist richtig, und er beantwortet die offene Frage sauber statt sie zu umgehen.**
Die Zuschnittsfunktion kann aus zwei Zeichenketten nicht erkennen, ob eine Vollersetzung vorliegt — jede Ableitung wäre die verbotene Größenschätzung. Also gibt die aufrufende Stelle diese Kenntnis herein, mit einem Standardwert, der alle bestehenden Aufrufer unverändert lässt. Drei der siebzehn Stellen bekommen die neue Kennzeichnung, vierzehn bleiben buchstabengleich. Ich habe nachgerechnet, dass die neue Zerlegung tatsächlich eine einzige zusammenhängende Spanne ergibt und dass die Anzeige dafür nicht angefasst werden muss.

**Der Punkt-Grenzfall verschwindet als Nebenwirkung, ohne Sonderbehandlung.**
Wo bisher eine leere Ersetzungsspanne entstand, steht künftig der Punkt selbst. Auch das habe ich selbst durchgerechnet, nicht dem Bericht entnommen.

**Eine der drei Stellen habe ich beim Nachlesen als nicht eindeutig erkannt.**
Der Ablehnungszweig ersetzt bei einfachem Text tatsächlich alles — bei einer Blockliste aber nur die betroffenen Blöcke und lässt die übrigen unberührt. Die Kennzeichnung wirkt jedoch auf Nachrichtenebene. Das bricht nichts, weil unveränderte Blöcke die Funktion sofort wieder verlassen, bevor die Kennzeichnung überhaupt gelesen wird — das trägt die Korrektheit an dieser Stelle, nicht die Klassifikation. > - Produktivcode-Diff gelesen: drei Dateien, 98 Zeilen, alle Änderungen im Rahmen
> - Alle fünf Prüfsammlungen selbst gefahren, jeweils null Fehlschläge
> - Das Messskript aus Meilenstein 1 gegen den reparierten Code erneut gefahren
> - Dabei überschriebenen historischen Bericht per Git zurückgesetzt
> - Recap für Meilenstein 3 ausgelöst, Timer 10 Minuten

**Die überzeugendste Prüfung war, das Messgerät von Meilenstein 1 gegen den reparierten Code zu halten.**
Es hatte vor dem Eingriff 97 Vollersetzungen gemeldet, davon 17 fälschlich als Teiländerung geführt. Nach dem Eingriff meldet dasselbe Skript 99 Vollersetzungen, davon null fälschlich geführt. Das Instrument wurde gebaut, bevor die Reparatur existierte, und liest jetzt genau null — ein Nachweis, den man nicht versehentlich passend hinbiegt. Die 43 echten Teiländerungen sind unverändert, das hat der Arbeiter mit einem Vorher-Nachher-Abgleich belegt.

**Beim Nachprüfen habe ich selbst einen Schaden angerichtet und wieder behoben.**
Mein erneuter Lauf des Messskripts hat den datierten Bericht von Meilenstein 1 überschrieben — die alten Zahlen 97 und 17 waren durch 99 und 0 ersetzt. Das ist genau die Datei, auf der die Prozessdokumentation als Beweisgrundlage steht. Ich habe sie über Git zurückgeholt und die Regel als Auflage in den Recap gegeben: ein Skript, das einen datierten Bericht erzeugt, darf nicht über seinen eigenen bereits festgeschriebenen Stand laufen. Eine Messung nach dem Eingriff bekommt einen neuen Dateinamen.

**Die drei gekennzeichneten Aufrufstellen sind jetzt einzeln begründet, statt nur eingeordnet.**
Beim Ablehnungszweig steht das Argument im Code, das die Korrektheit tatsächlich trägt: unveränderte Blöcke verlassen die Funktion, bevor die Kennzeichnung gelesen wird. Ohne diesen Satz hätte die nächste Änderung an dieser Stelle blind auf die Klassifikation vertraut.

**Nach dem Merge brauche ich dich für die letzte Instanz.**
Beide Reparaturen sitzen dann auf `integration`. Der laufende Proxy arbeitet mit einer eingefrorenen Kopie — erst ein Neustart nimmt sie auf. Danach löse ich beide Fälle aus: einen Aufruf, den du manuell in den Hintergrund schiebst, und einen, den ich selbst dort starte. Du liest im Proxy-Fenster ab, ob die ersetzte Meldung als ein durchgehend grüner Block ohne blasses Vorwort steht.

7	+# Full-replacement-aware `_extract_block_op`, 2026-07-29
8	+
9	+Milestone-3 fix: the M1 blast-radius measurement (same area, 2026-07-29) established that
10	+`_extract_block_op`'s common-prefix/suffix trim mis-renders 17 (of 97 measured) FULL-class ops as
11	+a 2-piece split when the replacement happens to share leading/trailing text with the original —
12	+live-observed as a background-launch ack rendering with the shared word `"Command"` unhighlighted
13	+on its own line, the rest green below. This entry records the fix and the design reasoning behind
14	+each choice, not just the diff.
15	+
16	+## Why the signal must come from the caller, not inferred from the two strings
17	+
18	+`_extract_block_op(before, after)` only ever receives two strings — it has no way to know which
19	+pass produced them or what that pass intended. The obvious alternative, inferring "whole-content
20	+replacement" from some ratio/size property of the two strings, was already ruled out by the M1
21	+measurement itself: FULL-class ops measured a `len(removed)/len(bt)` ratio range of
22	+`[0.973, 1.000]`, PARTIAL-class ops measured `[0.015, 1.000]` — the ranges overlap, so no
23	+threshold could separate the two classes without misclassifying real cases in both directions (a
24	+large SR block excised from a mostly-empty surrounding message legitimately scores near 1.0; a
25	+whole-block replacement whose text happens to share a long accidental prefix/suffix with the
26	+original would score below any reasonable cut). The only place that genuinely knows which case it
27	+is is the calling pass function itself — it either constructs new content independently of the
28	+old, or it excises a known chunk and keeps everything else. That knowledge has to be threaded in
29	+explicitly.
30	+
31	+## Why a default argument keeps 14 of 17 sites byte-identical
32	+
33	+`_extract_block_op` and `_ops_from_content_change` both gained a `full_replace: bool = False`
34	+parameter. Every one of the 17 real call sites in `message_passes.py`, plus 3 direct test-file
35	+callers found by grep, calls these functions with 2 positional arguments — none of them pass a
36	+third. Only 3 call sites were edited to add `full_replace=True` explicitly; the other 14 are
37	+textually and behaviorally untouched. This is why the PARTIAL-ops regression argument is
38	+"byte-identical by construction," not just "byte-identical because I tested it": the code path
39	+those 14 sites execute is the exact pre-milestone code, unreachable-different by construction, not
40	+merely observed-to-be-unchanged.
41	+
42	+## Why the rendering layer needed no change at all
43	+
44	+Hand-traced `apply_edit_to_spans`/`compose_block` (`diff_engine.py`) against the op
45	+`(0, before, after)` before writing any code: starting from `spans = [('equal', c0_text)]`, one
46	+full-block edit op at offset 0 covering the whole text splits that single equal span into exactly
47	+`[('stripped', before), ('injected', after)]` — one contiguous stripped span, one contiguous
48	+injected span, no `equal` fragment left over. `_render_span_content`
49	+(`proxy_display/render_messages.py`) already renders a single injected `(tag, text)` tuple as one
50	+contiguous colored block in its existing new-format branch. Nothing in either file needed to
51	+change; both were exercised, unmodified, by the regression guard and by re-running the M1 render
52	+harness against real corpus data post-fix, and produced the desired one-block render directly.
53	+
54	+## Per-site justification for the 3 flagged sites
55	+
56	+- `_apply_role_system_strip` — unambiguous: content is set to the literal `"."` unconditionally,
57	+  regardless of shape (`message_passes.py:66`). No caveat needed.
58	+- `_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip` — `_strip_bg_launch_ack` sets a matched block's whole text/content
59	+  field wholesale to `_build_launch_ack_replacement(text)`; every block it leaves alone is
60	+  appended by identity. Same early-return safety as the other two sites. This is the flagship case
61	+  the milestone was measured against.
62	+- `_apply_first_pass`'s rejection branch — the one site that is NOT uniformly full-replace at the
63	+  message level: `_strip_rejection_message` (`content_strip.py`) mutates PER-BLOCK for list
64	+  content, not the whole message at once, and can leave sibling blocks untouched. Verified by
65	+  reading the function directly: every block it actually changes is wholesale-set to the literal
66	+  `"."` (`content_strip.py:43`, `{**block, "content": "."}`), never partially edited in place, and
67	+  every block it leaves alone is appended by identity (`content_strip.py:45`) — so `bt==at`
68	+  exactly for those, and `_extract_block_op`'s `before==after` early-return fires before
69	+  `full_replace` is even consulted. The message-level flag is correct here specifically because
70	+  this pass has no per-block PARTIAL-edit path to protect against — not because the branch is
71	+  "FULL" in the abstract, but because the concrete mutation shape at this call site never produces
72	+  a changed block that isn't a wholesale swap. This distinction — the flag applied at message
73	+  level, the true correctness argument resting on a per-block property — is recorded directly in
74	+  the code comment at the call site, not only here.
75	+
76	+## The `.`-absorption edge case resolves as a side effect, not by special-casing
77	+
78	+No code was written to detect or handle the `.`-absorption case (`before='abc.', after='.'` →
79	+previously `injected=''`) specifically. It disappears automatically because
80	+`_apply_role_system_strip` is one of the 3 `full_replace=True` sites: the op becomes
81	+`(0, 'abc.', '.')` directly, bypassing the suffix-trim step that used to absorb the shared `.`
82	+into nothing. Confirmed against the 2 real occurrences found in the corpus (both
83	+`_apply_role_system_strip`, both text ending in a truncation-notice period): `injected` changed
84	+from `''` to `'.'` in both, with no special-case branch added anywhere in the fix.
85	+
86	+## Empirical regression evidence (as of 2026-07-29, 527 requests, 142 ops)
87	+
88	+Captured a full per-op dump (site, class, offset, removed, injected, before-text, after-text)
89	+using the M1 driving loop, once immediately before editing `src/`, once immediately after, on the
90	+same static corpus snapshot (527 requests both times — corpus did not grow between the two
91	+captures). Matched records by `(site, before_text, after_text)`:
92	+
93	+- **43/43 PARTIAL ops byte-identical** — 0 mismatches on `(offset, removed, injected)`.
94	+- **99/99 FULL ops now recorded as `(0, before_text, after_text)`** — 0 still trimmed, 0 wrong.
95	+  (99 rather than M1's originally-measured 97: the corpus grew by 2 FULL ops between the M1
96	+  measurement and this fix, both handled correctly by the same code path — no special-casing was
97	+  needed for the newly-arrived ones either.)
98	+
99	+As an end-to-end sanity check, the *unmodified* M1 blast-radius script
100	+(`dev/proxy_instrumentation/p1_measure_full_replacement_blast_radius.py`) was re-run against the
101	+fixed code — the same measurement instrument that quantified the defect before the fix now reports
102	+`FULL-class ops: 99, of which 0 currently trimmed` (was `97, of which 17 trimmed`). This
103	+confirms the fix from the same measurement angle the milestone was scoped against.
104	+
105	+**Constraint this session surfaced and must not be repeated:** re-running the M1 script this way
106	+initially overwrote `dev/proxy_instrumentation/md/full_replacement_blast_radius_20260729.md` in
107	+place with the post-fix numbers, clobbering the dated pre-fix snapshot that this entry (and the
108	+M1 process-docs entry) rest on as evidence. That file was reverted to its pre-fix committed state.
109	+A script that regenerates a dated report must never be re-run over its own already-committed
110	+output — a post-fix measurement, if ever wanted, belongs in a NEW dated report filename, never
111	+overwriting an existing one.
112	+
113	+## Verification boundary (as of 2026-07-29)
114	+
115	+Verified at integration level: real production functions (`_extract_block_op`,
116	+`_ops_from_content_change`, `_apply_role_system_strip`, `_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip`,
117	+`_apply_first_pass`, `compose_block`, `_render_span_content`) exercised directly against a real
118	+fixture and real corpus data, plus the full before/after op-dump diff described above. NOT
119	+verified against a restarted live proxy rendering a genuine background-launch ack in real time —
120	+the running proxy uses a frozen source copy and only picks up a source change after restart; that
121	+gate is still open.
122	+
123	+## Relevant Symbols / Paths
124	+
125	+- `_extract_block_op`, `_ops_from_content_change` (`src/proxy/rule_ops.py`) — `full_replace`
126	+  parameter, defaults preserve prior behavior for all untouched call sites
127	+- The 3 `full_replace=True` call sites (`src/proxy/message_passes.py`):
128	+  `_apply_role_system_strip`, `_apply_first_pass`'s rejection branch, `_apply_bg_launch_ack_strip`
129	+- `apply_edit_to_spans`, `compose_block` (`src/proxy/diff_engine.py`) — consumed unmodified
130	+- `_render_span_content` (`src/proxy_display/render_messages.py`) — consumed unmodified
131	+- Regression guard: Item 4q (`dev/proxy_dual_log/proxy_176_bg_launch_ack_tests.py`) — pins the op
132	+  shape and the composed span shape against the real launch-ack fixture
133	+- Measurement instrument re-run for confirmation:
134	+  `dev/proxy_instrumentation/p1_measure_full_replacement_blast_radius.py`

# Live observations of the proxy-side background messages, 2026-07-29

Orchestrator-side live session against a RUNNING proxy carrying the 2026-07-28/29 merged state
(the frozen source copy in place before this session's own fixes). Everything below was observed
by being the RECEIVING model — the forwarded content as it actually arrived, not read out of a log
or inferred from code. Recorded here because a running proxy is the only source for these
observations and the measurement/fix milestones of the same day could not produce them.

## Method

Ran a sentinel-controlled Bash counting loop (`while [ ! -f /tmp/stop-bg-loop ]`), had the user
manually background it mid-run, then terminated it by touching the sentinel — so both the launch
and the termination message were produced by a real CC background task, twice, once per launch
path. Separately started `sleep 600 && echo done` with `run_in_background=true` for the
agent-initiated path, and read a process-docs file containing a line-anchored, markdown-fenced
`<system-reminder>` example block through the Read tool for the quoted-SR question.

## Termination message — correct on BOTH launch paths

The wake-up arrived as the canonical 3 lines in both cases (agent-backgrounded and
user-backgrounded): the wake-up sentence, `Output: <path>`, `ID: <task id>`. No bare `'.'`,
nothing truncated. The two ids observed were `bsxpatpam` (user-backgrounded loop) and `bcexi2n0t`
(agent-started timer). This closes the previously-unverified `role='system'` plain-str delivery
question: the reworked path is not nuked on a live proxy.

## Launch acknowledgement — correct only on the agent-initiated path

Agent-initiated (`run_in_background=true`): the replacement fired, 3 lines, own `ID:` line.

User-manually-backgrounded: the replacement did NOT fire. What arrived was CC's unmodified original
text, with the id embedded mid-sentence and no separate `ID:` line:

```
Command was manually backgrounded by user with ID: bsxpatpam. Output is being written to: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-brunowinter2000-Documents-ai-monitor-cc/587284d6-c174-4432-a8d0-b5e2bcf10f0b/tasks/bsxpatpam.output
```

Cross-checked two independent ways: the text is exactly 220 characters, matching the block size the
proxy pane reported for that block (`220c`), so the ack is complete and genuinely ends after the
path — there is no trailing `. You will be notified when it completes…` sentence on this path.
`grep` for `manually backgrounded` across `src/proxy` returned 0 hits: this launch path was never
implemented, rather than implemented and broken.

## There is no third launch path — CC kills instead of backgrounding on timeout

Tested directly: a 400-second Bash loop with no `run_in_background` and no timeout override. CC did
NOT background it on hitting the limit — the call was killed at the 2-minute boundary
(`Command timed out after 2m 0s`, exit code 143), with the loop's own log confirming it stopped at
tick 120. So the launch-wording space is 2 wordings, not 3.

One loose end, unresolved: a third task output file (`b7gjft8ks.output`) appeared in the task
directory at the moment of that kill and was gone seconds later when read. CC evidently allocates
a task id before aborting; whether that ever produces a forwarded message could not be determined
from the receiving side.

## Quoted `<system-reminder>` block survives the strip passes

Read `process-docs/proxy_noise_strip/task_2026-05-30.md`, which embeds a verbatim, real-newline,
markdown-fenced env-context `<system-reminder>` block — line-anchored, i.e. exactly the shape the
SR strip passes used to remove out of quoted tool output. All 9 lines of the block arrived intact,
including the address and date inside it. The 2026-07-28 change stopping the SR strip family from
descending into `tool_result` holds on a live proxy.

## Pane rendering of the replaced launch ack — split across two lines

User-observed in the proxy pane (screenshots reviewed in-session): the replaced agent-initiated
launch ack rendered with the shared leading word `Command` unhighlighted on its own line, the
replacement text green on the lines below. The termination message rendered as one contiguous green
block — consistent with it sharing no leading word with the text it replaced.

## Verification boundary as of this session

The observations above describe the proxy state BEFORE this session's own fixes; the running proxy
uses a frozen source copy and only picks up source changes on restart. Consequently NOT verified
live: the second launch wording being recognized, and the replaced ack rendering as one contiguous
green span. Both were verified only at integration level (real corpus + real production functions)
in the same day's fix milestones. The live gate needs a proxy restart, then re-running exactly the
two launch paths above.

## Sources for CC's own message wordings

CC's launch/termination message texts are not documented anywhere externally — CC emits them, and
no vendor documentation covers them. The only two sources are the project's own recorded dual-log
corpus (`src/logs/dual_log/`) and a strings dump of the CC binary itself. The corpus answered the
wording question this session, so the binary dump was named as an option and not used; it remains
the route to enumerate all variants at once should a third wording ever be suspected.

**Die Sitzung ist abgeschlossen und alles ist gepusht.**
Der Stand auf `main` trägt beide Reparaturen, vier neue Prozesseinträge, zwei Messskripte mit ihren Berichten und die aktualisierte Modulkarte. Der Suchindex kennt die neuen Dokumente, die nächste Sitzung findet sie also über den Bereichsnamen.

**Was die nächste Sitzung als erstes braucht: einen Proxy-Neustart.**
Danach löse ich zwei Aufrufe aus — einen, den du manuell in den Hintergrund schiebst, einen, den ich selbst dort starte. Zu prüfen sind zwei Dinge: ob beide Startbestätigungen die Kennungszeile tragen, und ob die ersetzte Meldung im Fenster als ein durchgehend grüner Block ohne blasses Vorwort steht. Das sind die Abschlusstests von #51 und #52; danach können beide zu.

**Mein Prozesseintrag hält bewusst auch die eine ungelöste Spur fest.**
Beim abgebrochenen Langläufer legte Claude Code eine Task-Kennung an und entfernte sie sofort wieder. Von der Empfängerseite lässt sich nicht feststellen, ob daraus je eine Meldung wird. Falls das später relevant wird, steht die Beobachtung samt Dateinamen dort — sonst bleibt sie eine Fußnote.
